children: From Interface Markets to Market Agencements
从界面市场到市场装配
WHAT IS A MARKET?
什么是市场？

As we begin this investigation, it is important that my readers and I agree on the limitations of existing discourses and the need to explore new modes of understanding the thing we call a “market.” The purpose of this introductory chapter is to establish such an agreement so that we can move on to the novel answers that I would like to propose.
在开始这项考察时，重要的是，我与读者要就现有话语的局限、以及探索理解我们称之为“市场”之物的新方式的必要性达成一致。本章作为引论，其目的正是确立这样一种共识，以便我们随后能够转向我希望提出的那些新回答。
What, then, is a market?
那么，什么是市场？

In 1994, Alan Greenspan, then president of the Federal Reserve, believing he knew, said this: “There’s nothing involved in Federal regulation which makes it superior to market regulation.” A few years later, he pursued this line of reasoning even further: “Bank loan officers, in my experience, know far more about the risks and workings of their counterparties than do bank regulators.”

Only the obtuse do not change their minds, however. By 2008, as the financial crisis was devastating Western economies, this same man, Alan Greenspan, was called to a hearing by the US House of Representatives. By this point, he was almost a mere citizen. He repented. He did not feel responsible for what was happening; he did not seem to regret having made bad decisions. What seemed to hurt him the most was that he had thought he had known what markets were, what they did, and how to regulate them, whereas he had to come to realize that he knew almost nothing about how they work:
1994年，时任美联储（Federal Reserve）主席的艾伦·格林斯潘（Alan Greenspan）自以为知道答案，说了这样一番话：“联邦监管中没有任何东西使它优于市场监管。”几年后，他沿着这条推理走得更远：“以我的经验，银行信贷官员对其交易对手的风险和运作方式的了解，远多于银行监管者。”

然而，只有愚钝者才从不改变想法。到2008年，金融危机正在重创西方经济体，同一个人——艾伦·格林斯潘——被美国众议院（US House of Representatives）传唤参加听证会。此时，他几乎只是一位普通公民。他忏悔了。他并不觉得自己对正在发生的事负有责任；他似乎并不后悔做过糟糕的决定。最让他痛心的似乎是：他原以为自己知道市场是什么、市场做什么、如何监管市场，却不得不认识到，他对市场如何运作几乎一无所知：

I made a mistake in presuming that the self-interest of organizations, specif- ically banks and others, were such that they were best capable of protecting their own shareholders and their equity in the firms. . . . So the problem here is something which looked to be a very solid edifice, and, indeed, a critical pillar to market competition and free markets, did break down. And I think that, as I said, shocked me. I still do not fully understand why it happened and, obviously, to the extent that I figure out where it happened and why, I will change my views. If the facts change, I will change. . . . What I am saying to you is, yes, I found a flaw [in my ideology], I don’t know how significant or permanent it is, but I have been very distressed by that fact.

“我犯了一个错误，想当然地认为，组织——具体来说是银行及其他机构——的自身利益，会使它们最有能力保护自己的股东和公司中的股权。……所以，这里的问题在于，某个看上去非常坚固的结构，而且确实是市场竞争和自由市场的一根关键支柱，竟然垮掉了。我认为，正如我所说，这让我震惊。我仍然不完全明白它为什么发生；显然，只要我弄清楚它在哪里发生、为什么发生，我就会改变我的看法。如果事实变了，我也会变。……我要对你们说的是：是的，我在[我的意识形态]中发现了一个缺陷，我不知道它有多严重、是否会长期存在，但我一直为此深感不安。”
When influential experts such as Alan Greenspan begin to doubt their theories and admit that they do not really know what markets are or how they work, it is time for some reflection.

One of the principal difficulties to overcome is that the descriptions that attempt to account for market activity are so enormously diverse. Nevertheless, it seems feasible to me that we pull out a few elements from the array of existing descriptions that link them together in a coherent manner. These common elements form an implicit model that gives the word “market” its most common meaning. As a result, whoever uses the word “market,” either in ordinary conversation or for elaborating analytic theories, adopts this common meaning, which is largely shared, but rarely discussed. I call this distilled model of markets the “interface market.” In contrast, I will propose an alternative model, which I have named the “agencement model.”
It is my sincere hope that from now on, whenever theorists speak of markets or the market, they will begin to invoke the agencement model in place of the far less realistic interface model.
当艾伦·格林斯潘这样有影响力的专家开始怀疑自己的理论，承认自己并不真正知道市场是什么、如何运作时，就该进行反思了。

需要克服的主要困难之一是，试图说明市场活动的各种描述实在太过多样。不过，在我看来，从现有描述的阵列中抽出若干要素、以连贯的方式把它们联系起来，似乎是可行的。这些共同要素构成一个隐含模型，赋予“市场”一词最常见的含义。因此，无论谁使用“市场”一词——无论是在日常交谈中，还是在构建分析理论时——都采纳了这一大体上被共享、却鲜少被讨论的共同含义。我把这种提炼过的市场模型称为“界面市场”。与之相对，我将提出另一种模型，我称之为“装配模型”。
我真诚地希望，从今以后，理论家们每当谈到各类市场或市场这一整体时，都会开始援引装配模型，取代远不那么现实的界面模型。

This introductory chapter is dedicated to presenting the two models side by side to show their commonalities and their differences. I will abstain from discussing any other economic forms or their respective merits and will focus my attention exclusively on the notion of a market so as to better specify the object to which the word is supposed to refer.
I will also avoid conflating the terms “market economy” and “capitalism,” as is too often done.

I begin from the hypothesis that there have existed, there exist, and there could exist market forms that are not capitalist. The notion of market agencement should make it easier to decouple these terms.
本章作为引论，致力于并置呈现这两个模型，以显示它们的共同之处与差异。我将不讨论任何其他经济形式及其各自优点，而把注意力完全集中在市场概念上，以便更好地界定这个词所应指称的对象。
我也将避免像人们常做的那样，把“市场经济”与“资本主义”这两个术语混为一谈。
我的出发假设是：曾经存在、现在存在、并且可能存在非资本主义的市场形式。市场装配这一概念应当有助于把这些术语解耦。
THE INTERFACE MARKET MODEL
界面市场模型

Anyone hoping for a ready-to-use definition of a market will be discouraged by a systematic study of the academic or general literature. The problem is not a dearth of answers and definitions; it is their great abundance and the frequent contradictions.
任何希望得到一个现成市场定义的人，只要系统研读学术文献或一般文献，都会感到沮丧。问题不在于答案和定义匮乏，而在于它们数量庞大且常常相互矛盾。

The diversity can easily be explained if one allows that individual experiences of the market are not reducible to one another. Who would claim that a single definition encompasses what an Egyptian peasant feels as he discusses the price of a bale of cotton with a trader from Cairo,
and
does justice to the diverging work of famous and recognized economists such as Milton Friedman, Friedrich Hayek, Oliver Williamson, or Richard Nelson,
and

takes into account Monsanto’s maneuvers as it uses all available means to eliminate traditional agriculture? And yet who would dare contest that in referring to the market, each of the agents contributes to a series of questions that are shared and over which they are divided, but that the notion of a market helps to articulate? Everybody talks about the market. Everybody is pointing to different practices and different issues. However, each in their own way recognizes the existence of common stakes, even if some strive to elaborate theoretical models while others seek only to understand concrete practices.
只要承认各人对市场的个体经验彼此不可还原，这种多样性就很容易解释。谁会声称，一个单一的定义既能涵盖一位埃及农民与开罗商人讨论一包棉花价格时的感受，
又能
公允对待米尔顿·弗里德曼（Milton Friedman）、弗里德里希·哈耶克（Friedrich Hayek）、奥利弗·威廉姆森（Oliver Williamson）或理查德·纳尔逊（Richard Nelson）等著名且公认的经济学家各不相同的工作，
还能
把孟山都（Monsanto）用尽一切可用手段消灭传统农业的种种动作纳入考量？然而，谁又敢否认：在指称市场时，每个行动者都为一系列共同拥有却又使他们彼此分歧的问题作出了贡献，而市场概念有助于把这些问题的表述串联起来？人人都在谈论市场。人人指向的是不同的实践、不同的问题。然而，每个人都以各自的方式承认存在共同的利害，即便有些人致力于构建理论模型，另一些人只想理解具体实践。

To identify the common elements among the current concepts of markets, the only possible strategy is to follow the advice of Colette Depeyre and Hervé Dumez, who suggest we investigate the different uses of the word as a point of departure. In my study, I will pay equal attention to people who engage in markets and to professionals who study from the outside how markets work.

Although informatic tools exist that can scour the literature in bulk, the enterprise I will undertake can be executed without such an investment. One way to simplify the work without losing sight of the final objective is to follow a selection of specialists who have consecrated part of their energy to this work. There are economists, sociologists, and anthropologists who have in effect dedicated sustained efforts to pass from local, empirical observations to a stylized, abstracted, and generalizable account of markets. It is by reconstituting their strategies of abstraction and by verifying what is largely shared in the end that we should be able to sort out some common elements in the existing literature that define what I have called the interface model.
要找出当下各种市场概念中的共同要素，唯一可行的策略是听从科莱特·德佩尔（Colette Depeyre）和埃尔韦·迪梅兹（Hervé Dumez）的建议：把该词的不同用法作为出发点来考察。在我的研究中，我会同等关注投身市场的人，以及从外部研究市场如何运作的专业人士。

尽管存在能够批量检索文献的信息学工具，但我所要从事的工作无需这样的投入也能完成。一种既能简化工作、又不至于偏离最终目标的办法，是追随一批把部分精力奉献给这项工作的专家。确实有一些经济学家、社会学家和人类学家，持续付出努力，从地方性的经验观察走向对市场的简化、抽象且可概括的描述。正是通过重构他们的抽象策略，并核实最终在多大程度上形成共识，我们才应当能够从现有文献中梳理出若干共同要素，以界定我所说的界面模型。
FROM MARKET AS PLACE TOWARD ITS ABSTRACT REPRESENTATION

The most common, oldest, and most constant meaning of the word “market” refers to sites, generally public sites, covered or outdoors, where all sorts of merchants exhibit and sell foodstuffs and common household items. There are many examples of this form of market: the one in Chichicastenango that Simone de Beauvoir refers to in
The Mandarins
; the one in Lima that the economist Roger Guesnerie visits in his essential book on market economy;

the fairs in Champagne that, in the Middles Ages, with their currencies and charters, organized long-term European trade; flea markets; fish markets; a market in Marseille where Cuvier is said to have discovered the principles of his natural history; the Tsukiji market in Tokyo, which I used to visit in the early morning whenever I was in Japan, always dazzled by the streaming colors; the labyrinths of the souk in Sefrou that Clifford Geertz described so well;
the markets of Provence depicted by Michèle de La Pradelle and that appear in Gilbert Bécaud’s songs.
It would be tempting to extend the list — why not Wall Street or the Matif?
— and to start an inventory of the places where, since high antiquity, merchants and clients have met in person in order to render and preserve the singularity of each marketplace.
从作为场所的市场走向其抽象再现
“市场”一词最常见、最古老、也最恒久的含义，指的是场所，通常是公共场所，有顶棚或露天的，各种商人在那里展示并出售食品和日常家用物品。这种市场形式的例子很多：西蒙娜·德·波伏娃（Simone de Beauvoir）在《名士风流》（
The Mandarins
）中提到的奇奇卡斯特南戈（Chichicastenango）市场；经济学家罗歇·盖内里（Roger Guesnerie）在其关于市场经济的重要著作中造访的利马市场；
中世纪香槟地区的集市，那里凭借自己的货币与特许状，组织了欧洲的长期贸易；跳蚤市场；鱼市；据说居维叶（Cuvier）在其中发现其博物学原理的马赛市场；东京的筑地市场——每当我在日本，总会在清晨去那里，总被那流动的色彩晃得目眩；克利福德·格尔茨（Clifford Geertz）描绘得如此出色的塞夫鲁（Sefrou）露天集市（souk）迷宫；
米谢勒·德·拉普拉代尔（Michèle de La Pradelle）笔下的普罗旺斯集市，它们也出现在吉尔贝·贝科（Gilbert Bécaud）的歌声里。
人们会忍不住把这份清单继续延长——为什么不是华尔街或法国国际期货交易所（Matif）呢？
——并开始清点那些自远古以来商人与顾客亲身相遇、以呈现并保存每个市场场所独一性的地方。

The simple fact that the same word, “market,” is used to describe places and activities that are so different, across such different times and places, is an invitation to move beyond the specificities of each case and to bring out the common traits. The idea is to reach an underlying representation that captures the essential through successive abstractions. It is worth noting that the work of abstraction is not limited to specialists. Common thinking deploys expressions such as “the market of ideas,” “the dating market,” “putting oneself on the job market,” and so on. However, it is mostly experts, those who have chosen to study markets professionally, who have taken the most significant steps toward abstract representation. They have, in fact, followed the strategy of academic thinking. Whatever their claimed disciplinary affiliation, experts have sought to find common features of markets, shared across various configurations, in order to catch the unity of a given reality beyond contingencies and particular circumstances.

同一个词“市场”被用来描述在如此不同的时代和地点中如此不同的场所与活动，这一简单事实本身就邀请我们超越每个个案的独特性，揭示共同特征。其理念是通过层层抽象，抵达一种把握本质的深层再现。值得注意的是，抽象工作并不限于专家。日常思维也会使用“思想市场”“婚恋市场”“把自己投放进就业市场”之类的说法。然而，朝着抽象再现迈出最重要步伐的，主要是那些选择以研究市场为职业的专家。事实上，他们遵循的是学术思维的策略。无论其自称属于哪个学科，专家们都力求找到市场在各种配置中共享的共同特征，以便在偶然性与特殊情境之外把握某一既定现实的统一性。

When economist Roger Guesnerie left the market he visited in Lima in the 1970s, he resolved almost reluctantly to erase from the picture he drew of commercial relations “the ponchos, the chiseled faces of old Indians chewing coca, the cries of children around the mother carrying the youngest on her back in the traditional way,” noting that he had observed these things at one of the famous barter markets of the Andes, where goods were exchanged for goods and not money. He had a twinge of regret as he took on the task of distancing himself from what he saw, as any scientist worthy of the name must.

Guesnerie is not alone in having done this because every discipline imposes the same method. When Mark Granovetter analyzed the labor market in sociology, he endeavored to gradually reveal the underlying structure beyond events and observable encounters, tracing the networks of social relations and their morphology in order to give an account of the conditions in which transactions take place — in this case, hiring.
I could give many other references that would all show this movement of abstraction.
As I will show, this strategy of abstraction unfolds in three directions, thereby construing an overall coherence that permits one to speak of the construction of a model.

经济学家罗歇·盖内里在20世纪70年代离开他造访的利马市场时，几乎是不情愿地决定，从他描绘商业关系的图景中抹去“斗篷、嚼着古柯叶的印第安老人那刀刻般的面孔、围在按传统方式把最小的孩子背在背上的母亲身边的孩子们的喊叫声”；他注明，自己是在安第斯山脉著名的物物交换市场之一看到这些景象的，那里是货换货，而不是用货币交换。当他承担起与所见保持距离的任务时，他感到一阵遗憾——任何名副其实的科学家都必须如此。
盖内里并非唯一这样做的人，因为每个学科都强加同样的方法。马克·格兰诺维特（Mark Granovetter）在社会学中分析劳动力市场时，努力在事件与可观察的相遇之外逐步揭示底层结构，追踪社会关系网络及其形态，以说明交易发生的条件——在此情形中即雇用。
我还可以举出许多其他文献，它们都会显示这种抽象的运动。
正如我将要说明的，这一抽象策略朝三个方向展开，从而建构起一种整体连贯性，使人们能够谈论一个模型的建构。

First, the strategy emphasizes the idea of an abstract space in which relationships are themselves abstractions: they are established by encounters between agents defined as sellers and agents defined as buyers. The movement then insists that these relations are governed by mechanisms of competition. Finally, for these relationships to endure and for the market to be stabilized, it is judged necessary that rules, conventions, or, more largely, institutions come into existence.
第一，这一策略强调一个抽象空间的概念，其中的关系本身也是抽象的：它们由被界定为卖家的行动者与被界定为买家的行动者之间的相遇所建立。这一运动随后坚持认为，这些关系受竞争机制支配。最后，为使这些关系得以持续、使市场得以稳定，人们认为必须让规则、惯例，或者更宽泛地说，制度产生出来。

In my reading, these elements are common to the majority of scholarly representations of the market. They constitute a shared basis, a sort of greatest common denominator or core from which more sophisticated analyses (such as those offered by neoclassical economics or social-network sociology) are developed, particularly within economics and sociology. This stripped-back model, now widely taken for granted and rarely discussed, is a starting point from which, by gradually enriching it, everyone can elaborate their own conception of markets and their functioning. I propose to name this model the “interface market.” To identify the common constitutive elements, I will mobilize work that was mostly done by economists of different schools who were among the first to make explicit the categories that are largely adopted by everyone who is interested in discussing market activities and that are practically naturalized — think competition, supply and demand, or market structure. As we will see, establishing a common model will prove to be useful for highlighting, by contrast, the characteristics of my alternative model of market agencements.

依我的解读，这些要素为大多数关于市场的学术再现所共有。它们构成一个共同基础，一种最大公约数或核心；更精细的分析（例如新古典经济学或社会网络社会学所提供的分析）正是从这一基础发展而来，尤其在经济学和社会学内部。这个被剥离到最低限度的模型如今被广泛视为理所当然，鲜少受到讨论；它是一个起点，人人可以由此逐步充实，构建自己对市场及其运作的构想。我提议把这个模型命名为“界面市场”。为了找出共同的构成要素，我将调动主要由不同学派经济学家完成的工作——他们最早明确表述了那些被所有有兴趣讨论市场活动的人广泛采纳、并且实际上已被自然化的范畴：想想竞争、供给与需求，或市场结构。我们将会看到，确立一个共同模型，将有助于通过对比凸显我提出的另一种市场装配模型的特征。
FIRST ABSTRACTION: SELLERS, BUYERS, AND PLATFORM GOODS

Consider the work of economist Maurice Allais, which has greatly contributed to how we can think through the stakes of modeling and abstraction. For him, “the market” (note the definite article, which introduces a word that refers to a general category of things or beings) presents itself as a situation in which “groups of buyers and sellers are in continuous business relations and effect transactions spread over all sorts of products.”
Put forward in his
Cours d’économie générale

, this definition corresponds to minimal abstraction. It preserves the buyers and sellers of marketplaces (without yet speaking of supply and demand); it assigns a central role to the establishing of relations between buyers and sellers and to the ensuing transactions.
第一次抽象：卖家、买家与平台物品
考虑经济学家莫里斯·阿莱（Maurice Allais）的工作，它极大地影响了我们如何思考建模与抽象的利害。对他而言，“市场”（注意定冠词，它引入一个指称事物或存在者的一般范畴的词）呈现为这样一种情境：“买者群体与卖者群体处于持续的业务关系之中，并完成分布于各种产品之上的交易。”
这一界定出自他的《一般经济学教程》（
Cours d'économie générale
），对应最低限度的抽象。它保留了市场上的买者与卖者（尚未谈及供给与需求）；它把中心角色赋予买者与卖者之间关系的建立以及随之而来的交易。

In order to reach this first level of abstraction, the material sites that allow and provide the framework for markets have to be erased so that it becomes possible to focus only on the goods and the agents prepared to engage in transactions. Nothing is left of Lima, Chichicastenango, Tsukiji, or Marseille, the stalls or the instruments that allow for weighing and counting, the labyrinth of alleyways guiding customers’ wanderings, or the conversations between agents that lead to a possible agreement. What is foregrounded is the crowd of buyers and sellers, without geolocalizations, bereft of ponchos and chiseled faces. With no identity other than their role in the transaction, they are plunged into a dematerialized space.

要达到这第一个抽象层次，就必须抹去那些允许市场存在并为其提供框架的物质场所，以便只专注于物品以及准备进行交易的行动者。利马、奇奇卡斯特南戈、筑地或马赛都不复存在；摊位、用于称量和计数的器具不复存在；引导顾客游走的迷宫般小巷不复存在；行动者之间导向可能协议的交谈也不复存在。被推到前景的，是买者与卖者的人群，没有地理位置，失去了斗篷和刀刻般的面孔。除了在交易中的角色，他们没有任何身份，被投入一个去物质化的空间。
What is more, the existence of a population of buyers and a population of sellers implies that goods have already been developed to provoke the establishment of commercial transactions.

In the interface model, goods play a foundational role in the constitution and the setting in motion of these two populations by creating conditions for them to meet. Goods are, or can be, defined by the qualities (or attributes) that are attached to them and that determine their profile. The description of those qualities might be subject to debate. However, beyond the inevitable conflicts of interpretation they generate, goods constitute identifiable and stabilized things, localizable in time and space. Their existence is a given; they are already there, available. Regardless of how one describes agents, their skills, and their motivations and however one analyzes the structure of each of the populations (networks or separate atoms), what characterizes goods from an economic point of view is that they connect and coordinate these two populations of agents, the buyers and the sellers, while also maintaining their own autonomy.
此外，买者群体的存在与卖者群体的存在，意味着物品已经被发展出来，以促成商业交易的建立。

在界面模型中，物品通过为这两个群体创造相遇的条件，在它们的构成与启动中发挥奠基性作用。物品是——或可以是——由附着于其上、并决定其面貌的品质（或属性）来界定的。对这些品质的描述可能引发争议。然而，除了它们必然引发的解释冲突之外，物品构成了可识别、已稳定的事物，可以在时间与空间中被定位。它们的存在是给定的；它们已经在那里，可供使用。无论人们如何描述行动者、其技能与动机，也无论人们如何分析各个群体的结构（网络还是彼此分离的原子），从经济学观点看，物品的特征在于：它们连接并协调这两个行动者群体——买者与卖者——同时又保持自身的自主性。

To characterize this conception, we need only turn toward recent developments in neoclassical economics that propose the notion of platform goods to describe the growing role that goods play, a role that is no longer solely limited to configuring relationships between populations of buyers and sellers. The simplest and best-known example of such goods is the free news paper. The daily handed to subway commuters each morning as they go to work is financed by advertising inserted in the pages. The newspaper, as a good, puts three different “groups” of agents into relation: the advertising agencies who buy space, the users of public transportation who glance at the ads as they read the papers, and the company that conceives the newspaper, putting it together and distributing it. Using the term “platform” to designate such goods underscores that their function is to articulate several separate populations of agents. Economists have coined the term “multisided markets” to designate this type of market organization.

As defined by economists, these platform goods and their multisided markets have become more numerous. Initially developed to describe credit card markets, the model is now applied to mobile phones and video games. This proliferation is evidently linked to the growth of digital technology and what some are calling “datafication.”

要刻画这一构念，我们只需转向新古典经济学晚近的发展，它提出“平台物品”这一概念，用以描述物品所扮演的日益增长的角色——这一角色不再仅限于配置买者群体与卖者群体之间的关系。这类物品最简单、最著名的例子是免费报纸。每天早晨在地铁通勤者上班途中递到他们手中的日报，靠插入版面的广告来融资。报纸作为一种物品，把三个不同的行动者“群体”联系起来：购买版面的广告代理公司、在读报时瞥见广告的公共交通使用者，以及构思、编排并发行这份报纸的公司。用“平台”一词来指称这类物品，强调的是其功能在于把若干彼此分离的行动者群体联结起来。经济学家创造了“多边市场”一词来指称这种市场组织。
按照经济学家的界定，这类平台物品及其多边市场已越来越多。该模型最初为描述信用卡市场而发展出来，如今被应用于手机和电子游戏。这种扩散显然与数字技术的增长以及一些人所说的“数据化”（datafication）有关。

Paradoxically, the notion of platform goods perfectly accounts for the role played by all goods as we analyzed them earlier through the interface model, even though it was not initially imagined for these cases. The concept applies particularly well to more usual configurations in which there are only two distinct populations of agents — that is, two sides in the market. In all multisided markets as defined by economists, the principal function of goods is to articulate expectations, propositions, and requests that are external to the goods themselves. This is what makes it appropriate to redescribe goods as platforms. A platform good maintains the separation between several populations of agents while ensuring that they are put into relation with one another. Considering all goods as platforms when referring to multisided markets (including two-sided markets) is quite useful for capturing one of the essential characteristics of the common vision of markets that I am examining in this section.

悖论的是，平台物品这一概念完美地说明了所有物品所扮演的角色——正如我们先前通过界面模型所分析的那样——尽管它最初并非为这些情形而设想。这个概念尤其适用于更常见的配置，即只有两个彼此不同的行动者群体——也就是市场的两边。在经济学界定的所有多边市场中，物品的主要功能是联结外在于物品本身的期待、提议与请求。正因如此，才适合把物品重新描述为平台。平台物品维持着若干行动者群体之间的分离，同时确保它们彼此建立关系。在指称多边市场（包括双边市场）时把所有物品都视为平台，对于把握我本节所考察的市场共同观念的一项本质特征颇为有用。

This point is worth repeating. To call all shoes “platform shoes” captures one of the essential characteristics of the interface market model, even if multi sided market analysts wouldn’t do this themselves! Whether we’re speaking of shoes, books, automobiles, vegetables, free newspapers, Google and its ad exchanges, or bank cards, the only important thing is the capacity of these goods to put agents in relation to one another and to provoke encounters likely to end in a commercial transaction. In every case, the goods are taken as a given. Nothing is said, nothing has to be said, about the process that sets up the situation, a process that is considered to happen outside the market that, when successfully concluded, ends in the establishment of a market. This conceptualization is the shared minimal definition of markets that I am attempting to show. It is based on the following triptych: supply, demand, and goods offered. It therefore focuses on the relations that organize markets and on their structures.

这一点值得重复。把所有鞋都称为“厚底鞋”（platform shoes，字面意为“平台鞋”），恰恰抓住了界面市场模型的一项本质特征，尽管多边市场分析者自己并不会这么做！无论我们谈论的是鞋、书、汽车、蔬菜、免费报纸、谷歌（Google）及其广告交易平台，还是银行卡，唯一重要的是这些物品让行动者彼此建立关系、并促成可能以商业交易告终的相遇的能力。在每一种情形中，物品都被当作既定的。关于建立这一情境的过程，什么也没有说，也不必说什么；这个过程被认为发生在市场之外，一旦成功完成，便以市场的建立告终。这一概念化就是我试图展示的关于市场的共同最低限度定义。它基于以下三联体：供给、需求与所提供之物。因此，它聚焦于组织市场的关系及其结构。

A last remark. The notion of the platform is evidently polysemic. It has become a catch-all buzzword. In economics, a platform is generally defined as an intermediary that creates a market and/or assembles a group of users to facilitate economic or social exchange. In my way of thinking about objects, it is not illogical, therefore, to extend this same word, “platform,” to describe the role of goods as they are conceived in the interface market model, which also, in their own way, must bring agents together. If we follow this general and largely accepted definition, we would naturally also consider software companies such as Amazon, Uber, or Meetic to be platforms, since these enterprises act to bring together, to match, to marry. But as we will see in Chapter 4, which is devoted to how encounters are organized within market agencements, these two meanings must be disentangled.

最后一点说明。平台这一概念显然是多义的。它已成为一个包罗万象的流行词。在经济学中，平台一般被界定为一种中介，它创造市场并且/或者聚集一群使用者，以促进经济或社会交换。因此，按照我思考物的方式，把“平台”一词延伸用于描述界面市场模型所设想的物品角色，并不不合逻辑——那些物品也以各自的方式把行动者聚拢在一起。如果我们遵循这个一般且被广泛接受的定义，我们自然也会把亚马逊（Amazon）、优步（Uber）或 Meetic 这样的软件公司视为平台，因为这些企业的作用就是聚合、配对、撮合。但正如我们将在第4章——该章专门讨论市场装配内部如何组织相遇——中看到的，这两种含义必须被解缠。
SECOND ABSTRACTION: COMPETITION

The first abstraction says nothing precise about how markets are set in motion and says nothing about what impels their dynamism and their extension. The second strategy of abstraction in the interface model strives to achieve a higher level of generality by revealing what is common to concrete markets, despite their diversity: it adds that as a particular form of economic organization,
the
market is synonymous with competition.
第二次抽象：竞争
第一次抽象没有精确说明市场如何被启动，也没有说明是什么推动市场的活力与扩张。界面模型中的第二种抽象策略力求达到更高的普遍性层次，揭示具体市场尽管多样却共同具有的东西：它补充说，作为一种特殊的经济组织形式，
市场
等同于竞争。

Competition is the motor that sets the machine in motion and structures its functioning. Whether one opens an economics textbook, a treatise of economic sociology, or a work of anthropology, whether one listens to a high-ranked civil servant or a company boss, a union official or a judge charged with ruling on market compliance with regulations, one almost inevitably encounters the question of competition. This observation holds from Adam Smith, who saw in competition “the force which tends to equate market and natural prices,”

all the way to the most recent developments in economic theory. The study of markets has constantly revolved around the analysis of modalities of competition between agents and around the relation between competition and cooperation. With his pithy formulation, Fernand Braudel perfectly summarized what is taken to be an obvious, shared understanding on the subject, despite varying conceptions of the market:
the market is competition

. Almost two centuries ago, Antoine-Augustin Cournot had expressed it in just as striking a manner: “What economists understand by market is not a place where acquisitions and sales are made, but a whole territory whose parts are linked by relations of free competition.”

If Cournot’s definition has stayed on people’s minds, it is because it brings together in a single sentence both elements of the abstraction: the one that dematerializes the space and sets up the scene as one where supplies and demands confront each other (the first abstraction) and the one that makes competition the mainspring of this confrontation.
竞争是让这台机器运转起来、并塑造其运作方式的马达。无论翻开一本经济学教科书、一部经济社会学论著，还是一本人类学著作；无论听一位高级公务员、一位公司老板、一位工会干部，还是一位负责裁定市场是否遵守规章的法官说话，人们几乎不可避免地会遇到竞争问题。这一观察从亚当·斯密（Adam Smith）一直延续到经济理论的最新发展——斯密在竞争中看到了“一种使市场价格与自然价格趋于相等的力量”，
市场研究始终围绕着对行动者之间竞争形态的分析，以及竞争与合作关系的分析而展开。费尔南·布罗代尔（Fernand Braudel）以其简洁有力的表述，完美概括了人们在这一问题上视为显而易见、普遍共享的理解——尽管人们对市场的构想各不相同：
市场就是竞争
。近两个世纪前，安托万-奥古斯丁·古诺（Antoine-Augustin Cournot）以同样醒目的方式表达过这一点：“经济学家所理解的市场，并不是一个进行买卖的场所，而是一整片领土，其各部分由自由竞争关系联结起来。”
古诺的定义之所以留在人们心中，是因为它在一个句子里同时汇集了抽象的两个要素：其一是使空间去物质化、把场景设定为供给与需求相互对峙之所（第一次抽象）；其二是使竞争成为这种对峙的发条。

“Competition” does not have a single meaning. The best-known and widely spread conception is that of so-called neoclassical economics. Let us turn once again to Allais, who gives a simple, concrete definition: “Competition corresponds to a market situation in which each seller sells to the buyer who accepts the highest price and each buyer buys from the seller who offers the lowest price.”

This situation is a reference point for what has been called “pure” and “perfect” competition. As the definition implies, prices serve here as coordinating mechanisms: they constitute the criteria for agents’ decisions, and their perpetual adjustment ensures the existence of a viable equilibrium. Allais emphasizes that such a configuration is only rarely found in reality, but he desists from saying never. Imperfection rules in this lowly world, and the degrees of its intensity depend on circumstances. Indeed, numerous and powerful are the forces that are opposed to competition and tend to institute situations of monopoly. Allais provides a few examples: too few agents; consumers’ attachments to habits and insufficient information about products (he says brands too often mask this insufficiency); industrial concentration, aided by technical progress; pushing to expand factory size, as well as horizontal or vertical integration, which both in turn lead to the constitution of monopolies;
the financial power of certain agents (giving them the power to wait, analyze markets, practice dumping, and so on); the political power of certain agents; the importance of the state as a buyer.
“竞争”并没有唯一的含义。最著名、流传最广的构想是所谓新古典经济学的构想。让我们再次回到阿莱，他给出了一个简单而具体的定义：“竞争对应于这样一种市场情境：每个卖家都把商品卖给接受最高价格的买家，每个买家都从提供最低价格的卖家那里购买。”

这种情境是所谓“纯粹”竞争与“完全”竞争的参照点。正如定义所暗示的，价格在此充当协调机制：它们构成行动者决策的标准，而其持续调整确保存在一个可行的均衡。阿莱强调，这种配置在现实中很少见到，但他忍住不说“从未”出现。在这个低微的尘世中，不完美占据统治地位，其强度取决于具体情境。的确，反对竞争、倾向于制造垄断局面的力量众多而强大。阿莱举了几个例子：行动者太少；消费者对习惯的依附以及关于产品信息的不足（他说品牌往往掩盖了这种不足）；在技术进步助推下的产业集中；扩大工厂规模的压力，以及横向或纵向一体化，这两者又都会导致垄断的形成；
某些行动者的金融实力（使他们有能力等待、分析市场、实施倾销等等）；某些行动者的政治权力；国家作为买方的重要性。
Observable configurations fall somewhere between the opposite poles of perfect competition and perfect monopoly in an in-between ruled by what is customarily called “imperfect” competition.

The history of recent developments in neoclassical economics revolves around the analysis of mechanisms of imperfect competition (and in particular of the factors identified by Allais) and of the tools, notably mathematical ones (such as game theory) that make it possible to give an account of these mechanisms and to indicate how their (supposedly) negative effects might be mitigated. As all economics students learn, this normative demand is linked to the hypothesis that the allocation of resources is considered optimal, or according to the less optimistic, efficient, when it is satisfied.
可观察的配置落在完全竞争与完全垄断这两个对立极之间的某个位置，处于一个由通常所谓“不完全”竞争所支配的中间地带。
新古典经济学晚近发展的历史，围绕着对不完全竞争机制（尤其是阿莱所识别的那些因素）的分析，也围绕着对相关工具——特别是数学工具（如博弈论）——的分析而展开；这些工具使人们能够说明这些机制，并指出如何缓解其（据称的）负面效应。正如所有经济学学生所学到的，这一规范性要求与如下假设相联系：当这一要求得到满足时，资源配置就被视为最优的，或者按照不那么乐观的说法，是有效率的。

In my inquiry, I do not intend to privilege the neoclassical conception of competition in any way. Whatever its theoretical value may be, it provides only one among several visions of the concrete forms competition can take. (I will discuss this in greater detail in Chapter 8, where I examine the case of financial markets and the economy of climate change.)
在我的考察中，我无意以任何方式偏重新古典的竞争构想。无论其理论价值如何，它只是关于竞争可能采取的具体形式的若干视野之一。（我将在第8章更详细地讨论这一点，那里我考察金融市场与气候变化经济的案例。）

One could easily illustrate the existence of many other analyses of competition. They frequently start from the notion of pure and perfect competition elaborated (and imposed as the reference model) by neoclassical economics. Many then go on to highlight the model’s lack of realism, showing that in reality, imperfections dominate. Some scholars consider that imperfections are due to social networks that frame relationships between agents, thereby constraining their behavior.

Some locate imperfection in the unequal distribution of capital and the relations of domination this produces. To yet others, it is the institutional regulations or conventions that narrowly define the modalities of competition.
人们很容易举例说明还存在着许多其他竞争分析。这些分析常常从新古典经济学所阐发（并作为参照模型强加）的纯粹完全竞争概念出发。许多分析随后着重指出该模型缺乏现实性，表明在现实中，不完美占据主导。一些学者认为，不完美源于框定行动者之间关系、从而约束其行为的社会网络。
一些人把不完美归因于资本的不平等分配以及由此产生的支配关系。还有一些人则认为，是制度性的规章或惯例狭隘地界定了竞争的形式。

Lastly, I would like to point to the fairly widespread vision proposed by the evolutionary economists, who have contributed in an original manner to the analysis of the role of technical progress and innovation in the dynamic of economic activities. They, too, consider competition to be the principal motor of economic activities. However, instead of putting agents and prices at the center of the competitive device, they consider the confrontation between a wider range of forces. They take into account agents and the supplies and demands they are supposed to express or to trigger, but they also consider that behind those entities, doing battle with one another, hybridizing, spreading, or disappearing, are technologies, skills, rules of the game, routines, know-how, and capacities for innovation that are simply using human agents or goods as vectors. The analogy with sociobiology, sometimes explicit, is obvious: sociobiology indeed asserts that genes at war with one another use human organisms in order to materialize their advantage. This conception of competition, as well as the processes of mutation and selection it implies, has the virtue of attributing an essential role to both agents and objects. According to the usual conceptions of competition, products are seen as passive objects whose role is simply to make possible the encounter between supplies and demands; in evolutionary economics, goods play a more active role in the dynamic of competition through their constant transformation. Goods and their technological trajectories orient, frame, and stimulate commercial activity.

最后，我想指出演化经济学家提出的一个相当普遍的视野，他们以原创的方式贡献了对技术进步与创新在经济活动动态中之作用的分析。他们也认为竞争是经济活动的主要马达。然而，他们不是把行动者和价格置于竞争装置的中心，而是考虑更广泛的力量之间的对峙。他们考虑行动者，以及行动者被设想为表达或引发的供给与需求；但他们也认为，在这些实体背后彼此交战、杂交、扩散或消失的，是技术、技能、游戏规则、惯例、诀窍和创新能力——它们只是把人类行动者或物品当作载体。与社会生物学的类比——有时是明确道出的——显而易见：社会生物学确实断言，彼此交战的基因利用人类有机体来实现自身的优势。这种竞争构想以及它所隐含的变异与选择过程，其优点在于把本质性的角色同时赋予行动者和对象。按照通常的竞争构想，产品被视为被动的对象，其作用仅仅是使供给与需求之间的相遇成为可能；而在演化经济学中，物品通过其持续转变，在竞争动态中扮演更为主动的角色。物品及其技术轨迹引导、框定并刺激商业活动。

In an economy characterized by the rampant proliferation of products whose number, ephemeral character, perpetual renewal, and infinite differentiation provoke gridlock and congestion, it is not absurd to describe a market as a process of mutation and selection between goods fighting for their own survival, where agents are left to adapt as intelligently as possible to the logic that organizes these variations.
在一个以产品的疯狂增殖为特征的经济中——产品的数量、短命性、不断更新与无限差异化造成僵局与拥堵——把市场描述为物品之间为自身生存而斗争、进行变异与选择的过程，并不荒谬；在这一过程中，行动者只能尽可能聪明地适应组织这些变异的逻辑。

In any case, regardless of the definition of the competition that is chosen, the structure proposed by the first abstraction remains untouched: the universe of goods is left outside the universe of agents, whoever they may be.
无论如何，无论选择哪种竞争定义，第一次抽象所提出的结构都原封不动：物品的宇宙被留在行动者的宇宙之外，无论这些行动者是谁。

Likewise for the role of innovation, which is viewed as a response to steep competition that would end in ruinous consequences for the loser if it were to continue for too long. By innovating, companies are supposed to reduce competition, or at least attenuate its most devastating consequences. In the interface market model, innovation is impelled by competition. This hypothesis leads to a principal interest in synergies that can be deployed by companies to assure themselves control over this competitive advantage: investments consecrated to in-house research and development, patenting, technology purchases, subcontracting contracts, start-up acquisitions, mergers, or even participation in cooperative networks such as academic research.
创新的角色同样如此：创新被视为对激烈竞争的一种回应；如果竞争持续过久，就会给失败者带来毁灭性后果。通过创新，企业被认为能够减少竞争，或至少削弱其最具破坏性的后果。在界面市场模型中，创新由竞争驱动。这一假设使人们主要关注企业为掌控这种竞争优势而能够部署的协同效应：投入内部研发的投资、申请专利、购买技术、分包合同、收购初创企业、并购，甚至参与学术研究之类的合作网络。

Since Joseph Schumpeter, one of the first scholars interested in this topic, one of the most often asked questions within the interface market model is about the impact of competition on innovation. The concrete activities devoted to the design and qualification of goods are considered to be on the fringes of the market per se. This work, which is at the heart of the market dynamics, is never mentioned or discussed in the literature. It is mentioned only to assess its cost or chances of success. As we will see later on, in the market agencement model, the role of competition is entirely the inverse. Competition cannot exist outside of innovation strategies.

自约瑟夫·熊彼特（Joseph Schumpeter）——最早关注这一主题的学者之一——以来，界面市场模型中最常被提出的问题之一，就是竞争对创新的影响。致力于设计物品并界定其品质的具体活动，被视为处于市场本身的边缘。这项工作处于市场动态的核心，却在文献中从未被提及或讨论。它被提到，只是为了评估其成本或成功机会。正如我们稍后将看到的，在市场装配模型中，竞争的作用完全相反。竞争不可能存在于创新策略之外。
THIRD ABSTRACTION: INSTITUTIONS

The market cannot be reduced to one-off and random encounters. It must also organize and ensure multiple and repeated transactions. These words are largely synonymous with and summed up by Allais’s expression “continuous relations,” which points toward the idea that there are stable structures in place that guarantee the organized recurrence of transactions. The third abstraction, which renders explicit the conditions that ensure stability, brings about the notion of institutions. This idea was notably developed and enriched by (neo)institutionalist currents of thought. As elegantly summarized by economists Benjamin Coriat and Olivier Weinstein, “The market exists insofar as
sustainable structures
are set up that frame
multiple
and
repeated
transactions in such a way that, beyond the accomplishment of each particular transaction, a relative continuity in the nature of relations between economic agents is ensured.”
第三次抽象：制度

市场不能被化约为一次性、随机的相遇。它还必须组织并确保多次、反复的交易。这些说法在很大程度上与阿莱的“持续关系”一语同义，并可由该语概括；它指向这样一种观念：存在着稳定的结构，保证交易有组织地反复发生。第三次抽象明确陈述了确保稳定性的条件，引出了制度的概念。这一观念尤其由（新）制度主义思潮发展和丰富。正如经济学家本雅明·科里亚（Benjamin Coriat）和奥利维耶·温斯坦（Olivier Weinstein）的优雅概括：“市场的存在，在于建立起
可持续的结构
，以框定
多次
反复
的交易，从而使每一笔特定交易的完成之外，经济行动者之间关系的性质仍能保持相对的连续性。”

It would be no exaggeration to point out that the vast majority of those interested in markets adopt this point of view. All viable markets require rules, private or public conventions, and laws or regulations that are shared and apply to all participants. The market, experts have concluded, is an institution.
可以毫不夸张地指出，绝大多数对市场感兴趣的人都采纳这一观点。所有可行的市场都需要规则、私人或公共的惯例，以及为所有参与者共享并适用的法律或规章。专家们由此得出结论：市场是一种制度。

Money is one of the central elements of this institutional apparatus. Rules accompany its creation, circulation, and uses, as well as the organizations that take charge of its elaboration and monitor its applications.

Nevertheless, the idea of necessary recourse to monetary payments has been left out of the analysis. Some authors used to consider barter, a practice of exchange without monetary compensation, to be at the heart of the notion of the market. According to them, it is irrelevant whether or not a payment with money takes place: money is introduced just to facilitate commercial exchanges when the number of agents (buyers and sellers) and the number of goods circulating grow beyond a certain threshold and the complexity of the organization of relations is such that barter becomes impracticable and inefficient on a large scale. Since for them the function of money is purely instrumental, they consider its use to have no effect on the nature and unfolding of the transactions. This conception of money, which has long been endorsed by the majority of economists interested in markets, is no longer tenable because there is no serious ethnographic research to support it. Scholars should be restricting the term “market” to economic organizations in which transfers of property between sellers and buyers are effected against monetary payment because it is quite impossible to prove the historical solidity of the hypothesis according to which monetary payment progressively replaced barter. As a matter of fact, money probably did not appear as a simple technical tool exclusively designed to facilitate exchanges and cope with complexity. Recent interventions in economic anthropology incite us to give up the tempting, but vain quest for origins and to focus instead on existing arrangements and the mechanisms of their transformation and to abandon the hope of being able to validate a genealogy according to which barter (or debt) is money’s ancestor.
货币是这一制度装置的核心要素之一。规则伴随着货币的创造、流通与使用，也伴随着负责货币创设并监督其使用的各类组织。

然而，必须诉诸货币支付这一观念却被排除在分析之外。一些作者过去认为，物物交换——一种没有货币补偿的交换实践——处于市场概念的核心。在他们看来，是否用货币支付无关紧要：货币的引入只是为了便利商业交换——当行动者（买者与卖者）的数量与流通物品的数量增长超过某一阈值，关系组织的复杂性使物物交换在大规模上变得不可行、无效率时，货币才出现。既然对他们而言货币的功能纯粹是工具性的，他们认为货币的使用对交易的性质与展开没有影响。这种货币观长期得到大多数对市场感兴趣的经济学家的认可，但如今已站不住脚，因为没有严肃的民族志研究支持它。学者们应当把“市场”一词限定于这样的经济组织：在其中，卖者与买者之间的财产转移以货币支付为对价而实现；因为要证明“货币支付逐步取代了物物交换”这一假设在历史上的坚实性，是完全不可能的。事实上，货币很可能并不是作为一种单纯的技术工具出现的，并非专为便利交换、应对复杂性而设计。经济人类学晚近的介入促使我们放弃那种诱人却徒劳的寻源冲动，转而关注现有的安排及其转变机制，并放弃这样一种希望：能够验证一种把物物交换（或债务）视为货币祖先的谱系。

Moreover, and this point is extremely important in my view, in making recourse to money as a central element in what is named a market, most specialists actually jettison the notion of exchange and its implicit association with solidarity: to speak of market exchange is nothing short of confusing.
This is why I propose that we acknowledge money as an essential element of the interface model.
此外——在我看来这一点极其重要——在把货币当作所谓市场的核心要素时，大多数专家实际上抛弃了交换概念及其与团结的隐含关联：谈论“市场交换”不啻于制造混乱。
这就是为什么我提议，我们应当承认货币是界面模型的一个本质要素。

As for rules, another form of institution, the number and content vary from expert to expert. All agree, however, that commercial institutions must ensure that once a transaction is realized, buyer and seller are clear of obligations: “Production and exchange could not have developed without a legal regime that puts in place a sufficiently efficient barrier against the risk of spoliation.”
This requires that property rights be defined and that the conditions of their transfer be strictly overseen and guaranteed.
Beyond these rules (deemed
constitutive
), one can imagine many other rules (considered
regulative
) that frame, for instance, competition, product certification, or the determination of working periods.
至于规则——另一种形式的制度——其数量与内容因专家而异。然而所有人都同意，商业制度必须确保：一旦交易实现，买者与卖者就摆脱了义务：“如果没有一种法律制度对掠夺风险设置足够有效的屏障，生产与交换就不可能发展。”
这要求界定财产权，并严格监督和保障财产权转移的条件。
在这些（被视为
构成性
的）规则之外，还可以设想许多其他（被视为
调节性
的）规则，例如框定竞争、产品认证或劳动时间规定的规则。

A final point merits attention. Increasing generalization is aided by the introduction of supply and demand, two notions that seem obvious to the point of being naturalized. Buyers and sellers, who are the only observables in marketplaces, are replaced by the forces of supply and demand they are taken to formulate, even though they rarely do formulate them. In the end, after these are aggregated, the abstraction speaks only of global supply and demand. Schumpeter noted that this movement of abstraction, which seems so simple and obvious (that is, the assumption that a purchase results from the encounter between one demand and one offer), was slowly constituted through numerous efforts spread out over more than a century. Once adopted, the two complementary notions of global supply and demand can be quantified and represented in charts. They enter into common expressions such as “decline in demand,” “surplus supply,” or the “crossed elasticity of demand.” The entities further become manipulable and can be the object of political strategies and targeted policies. Thus, we speak of sustaining demand, increasing supply, or growing parts of the market that favor competition and innovation.

最后一点值得注意。日益增长的普遍化得益于供给与需求这两个概念的引入——它们显得如此显而易见，以至于已被自然化。买者与卖者是市场中唯一可观察的东西，却被认为由他们所表述的供给与需求力量所取代，尽管他们很少真的表述这些力量。最终，在这些力量被加总之后，抽象所谈论的只剩总体供给与总体需求。熊彼特注意到，这一抽象运动——看似如此简单明了（即购买源于一项需求与一项供给的相遇这一假设）——是经过一个多世纪中无数努力才缓慢形成的。一旦被采纳，总体供给与总体需求这两个互补的概念就可以被量化，并在图表中表示。它们进入“需求下降”“供给过剩”或“需求交叉弹性”之类的常见表达。这些实体进一步变得可操作，可以成为政治策略和有针对性的政策的对象。于是，我们谈论维持需求、增加供给，或扩大市场中有利于竞争与创新的部分。

This third set of abstractions is essential. Complementing and amplifying the realism of the two preceding abstractions, it permits us to speak in a coherent fashion of the market as a general entity while at the same time leaving the door open to a wide variety of descriptions that depend upon the precise manner in which the institutional frameworks are defined.
第三组抽象至关重要。它补充并放大了前两次抽象的现实性，使我们能够以连贯的方式把市场作为一个一般实体来谈论，同时又为多种多样的描述敞开大门——这些描述取决于制度框架被界定的精确方式。

The triple movement of abstraction outlined above leads to a minimal description of market activities and organizations that I’ve proposed we call the interface model of the market. The reference, often implicit, to this model (
n

Everything around us unfolds as if the ordinary meaning of the word “market” should be conflated with this model. Rendered so unproblematic, the word is frequently taken up in more complex theoretical constructions as if its meaning can be taken for granted. Among the most influential thinkers and writers, rare are the individuals who would openly endorse this minimal definition, having never fully discussed it.
以上勾勒的三重抽象运动，导向对市场活动与市场组织的一种最低限度描述，我提议称之为市场的界面模型。对这一模型（

The Great Transformation

, acknowledges the importance of examining the organizational forms that support economic activities. But in contrast to Polanyi, who merely describes the diversity of forms, he explains it by introducing the hypothesis of universal economic behavior in humans: all human agents will pursue maximal gains by managing transaction costs. This straightforward explanation must nevertheless rely on the minimal definition of markets. Without saying so explicitly, North takes in Polanyi’s own definition of a market while taking the opportunity to make it very specific and restrictive: markets are institutions that make prices. North adds, in passing, that such markets can exist only under certain poorly understood conditions that must include the following features: a number of significant buyers and sellers, a set of (clearly defined) goods, agreement on the medium of exchange, and enforcement of property rights. That is all he says. Even though North is among the rare economists taking an interest in the specific nature of markets as organizational forms, he is nevertheless content to cement in place a minimal definition taken from standard economic thinking that fixates upon autonomous offers of supply and demand, well-stabilized goods, and prices that supposedly fluctuate upon the confrontation of supply and demand.

The Great Transformation
