Harrison White, one of the founders of the new economic sociology and of network analysis, confirms this: “A market is a social arena in which buyers and sellers meet. But for buyers and sellers to exist, a product has to exist and someone has to produce it.”
Viviana Zelizer, an American sociologist with profound influence in economic anthropology, concurs: “Markets are sets of social relations in which actors transfer goods and services.”

These three authors, who could not be more different from one another (and I could quote many others), share the same motif — that of the interface market — as they weave, embroider, and stretch their respective theoretical webs. Likewise, this model has served and continues to serve as the implicit and quasi-unique reference in public policy circles that seek to regulate market competition.
新经济社会学与网络分析的奠基人之一哈里森·怀特（Harrison White）确认了这一点：“市场是买者与卖者相遇的社会竞技场。但要存在买者与卖者，就必须存在产品，并且必须有人生产它。”
在经济人类学中影响深远的美国社会学家维维安娜·泽利泽（Viviana Zelizer）也表示赞同：“市场是行动者转移物品与服务的一套套社会关系。”
这三位作者彼此再不同不过（我还可以引用许多其他人），却共享同一个母题——界面市场的母题——同时各自编织、刺绣、拉伸自己的理论之网。同样，这一模型曾经、并且继续在试图监管市场竞争的公共政策圈中充当隐含的、几乎是唯一的参照。

Far from me is it to say that all those who have studied markets up to now are in error. As the rest of this book unfolds, I will constantly make reference to their work. But as we will see in the next section, this conception of the market, the market interface model, gives an incomplete and too narrow view of market organizations. This is why I prefer to resort to the market agencement model that I am now presenting. This shift is all the more timely with the increased commodification of living beings and the explosion of digital technology, where the interface market model has become an obstacle to the analysis of novel market activities.
我绝非要说，迄今为止所有研究市场的人都错了。随着本书其余部分的展开，我会不断参照他们的工作。但正如我们将在下一节看到的，这种市场构想——市场界面模型——对市场组织给出了一种不完整且过于狭窄的看法。这就是为什么我更愿意诉诸我现在要呈现的市场装配模型。随着生命体商品化的加剧与数字技术的爆炸，这一转向尤为及时：在这些领域，界面市场模型已成为分析新型市场活动的障碍。

The ambition of this book is to change the specific traits of markets that come to mind when we discuss market activities, such that we effectively have a new meaning to associate with the word “market” when it is used in shorthand to refer to market activities.
本书的抱负，是改变我们讨论市场活动时浮现在脑中的那些具体市场特征，使我们实际上能为“市场”一词赋予新的含义——当它被当作指称市场活动的简称使用时。
TOWARD THE MODEL OF MARKET AGENCEMENTS
走向市场装配模型

To isolate the lacunas that the agencement model must fill, the simplest strategy is to establish a list of the contributions and limits of the interface model it is designed to replace. Let’s begin by pulling out the fundamental contributions that cannot be jettisoned.
要厘清装配（agencement）模型必须填补哪些空缺，最简单的策略，是列出一份清单，说明它所要取代的界面模型有哪些贡献与局限。让我们先抽出那些不可抛弃的根本贡献。

The first contribution relates to the distinction that the interface market introduces between agents and goods. To establish a market, it is necessary to divide the constitutive entities into two great groups — the subjects (the agents) who participate directly or indirectly in initiating and executing transactions and the objects (the goods in all their various forms) upon which the transactions occur; or, translated into the language of Western law, which guarantees this separation, the persons and the other things. Without this great divide, the transaction is not possible.
第一项贡献，涉及界面市场在行动者与物品之间引入的区分。要建立市场，就必须把构成性实体划分为两大组：直接或间接参与发起与执行交易的主体（行动者），以及交易发生于其上的客体（各种形式的物品）；或者，用保障这一分离的西方法律语言来说，就是人与其他物。没有这道大分界，交易便不可能。

The second contribution is that the transaction consists of a transfer, or if we prefer, a commutation, of property rights. As a consequence, these must be defined in a sufficiently precise manner, must be defended, and are susceptible to contestation. The third contribution is to note that relationships of competition develop between the different agents. Using all legal means at their disposal, the game is to garner control over the establishment of new transactions.
第二项贡献在于：交易由财产权的转移构成，或者，若我们愿意这样说，由财产权的转换构成。因此，财产权必须以足够精确的方式得到界定，必须受到维护，并且可能招致争议。第三项贡献是指出：不同行动者之间会发展出竞争关系。这场博弈的目标，是运用他们所能支配的一切合法手段，夺取对新交易之建立的掌控。

Lastly, the fourth contribution concerns the proper qualification of commercial transactions. The idea that this can be assimilated with exchange is abandoned, and with it the expression “market exchange.” A commercial transaction simply consists of monetary payment, after which the agents are quits.
最后，第四项贡献关乎对商业交易的恰当定性。那种认为商业交易可与交换相等同的观念被放弃，“市场交换”这一说法也随之被放弃。商业交易仅仅由货币支付构成；支付之后，行动者便两清了。

The different contributions of the interface market, contributions that I take up in turn, should not mask their true insufficiencies, which I will present in a synthetic manner, one by one, in the lines that follow:
a) they do not take into account the material composition of market activities;

b) they bracket out the coconstructive process of creating supply and demand, which leads to underestimating the crucial role played by bilateral transactions and the initiation of these transactions;
c) they create unrealism through the concepts of aggregated supply and demand and bring about difficulties in comprehending the actual mechanisms for establishing prices;
d) they create a total impasse on the complex processes that result in a separation between agents and goods;
e) the hypothesis that goods are platforms precludes us from recognizing they are processes;
f) and lastly, they imply a description of agents that underestimates their diversity, heterogeneity, and plasticity.
界面市场的这些不同贡献——我将依次承接——不应掩盖它们真正的不足。下面，我将以综合的方式逐条呈现这些不足：
a) 它们没有考虑市场活动的物质构成；
b) 它们把创造供给与需求的共同建构过程括置在外，从而低估了双边交易以及这些交易之发起所扮演的关键角色；
c) 它们通过加总的供给与需求概念制造出不切实际之处，并给理解价格确立的实际机制带来困难；
d) 它们完全无法说明那些使行动者与物品相分离的复杂过程；
e) 物品即平台的假设，使我们无法承认物品是过程；
f) 最后，它们所隐含的对行动者的描述，低估了行动者的多样性、异质性与可塑性。

The agencement model has been conceived to integrate all of these contributions and also to respond to their insufficiencies. But before diving into its detailed analysis, it is useful to show in broad strokes how it reworks some of the hypotheses of the interface market and thus provides a different perspective from most existing analyses.
装配模型的构思，旨在整合上述全部贡献，同时回应它们的不足。但在深入分析其细节之前，先粗略勾勒它如何重铸界面市场的某些假设、从而提供一种不同于大多数既有分析的视角，是有益的。
KEY ROLE OF THE MATERIAL COMPONENT

The material component plays an essential part in commercial activities. This assertion is in stark contrast not only with the model of interface markets, but also with the economic or sociological analyses that have up to now built on it. Rules, conventions, norms, and values, the nature of laws, the forms of social-relationship networks are, as we noted, so many variables, alongside those of need, the calculation of interests, the search for distinctiveness, and the desire for imitation that analysts invoke to give an account both of the ways markets function and of the diversity of their forms of organization.
In principle, nothing prevents us from including material devices in the definition and description of institutions, but it is a fact that this option is only rarely chosen.
For a social sciences expert, whether an economist, a sociologist, or an anthropologist, institutions, psychological wellsprings, or cultural values are often “realities without bodies.”
物质组成部分的关键作用
物质组成部分在商业活动中扮演本质性的角色。这一论断不仅与界面市场模型形成鲜明对照，也与迄今为止以该模型为基础的经济学或社会学分析形成鲜明对照。规则、惯例、规范与价值，法律的性质，社会关系网络的形式，正如我们已指出的，都是分析者援引的诸多变量——与需要、利益计算、对独特性的追求以及对模仿的欲望并列——用以说明市场的运作方式及其组织形式的多样性。
原则上，没有什么阻止我们把物质装置纳入制度的定义与描述之中，但事实是，这一选项很少被选中。
对于社会科学专家——无论是经济学家、社会学家还是人类学家——制度、心理源泉或文化价值往往是“没有身体的实在”。

We cannot be satisfied with such bracketing. Max Weber’s observation should be taken seriously as that of one of the rare authors to have long ago suggested the active role of the material component in the organization and accomplishment of transactions. According to Weber, the material component is not there simply to serve as a backdrop for interactions that are reducible to pure social relations; it does not simply furnish resources to these relations. “It is the physical assemblages that allow the emergence and accomplishments of one of the distinctive characteristics of commercial activities: bargaining.”
This formulation is precious because we find in it not only notions such as emergence and material
assemblages
, to which we will return throughout this book, but also the clearest and most direct possible affirmation that these material assemblages contribute to formatting commercial transactions.
我们不能满足于这样的括置。马克斯·韦伯（Max Weber）的观察应当被认真对待：他是很久以前就提示物质组成部分在交易的组织与完成中具有主动作用的少数作者之一。按照韦伯的看法，物质组成部分并非只是充当那些可化约为纯粹社会关系之互动的背景；它也不只是为这些关系提供资源。“正是物理性的
组合体
，使商业活动的一项独特特征——讨价还价——得以涌现并得以完成。”
这一表述弥足珍贵，因为我们在其中不仅发现涌现、物质组合体等概念——本书将不断回到这些概念——而且发现尽可能最清晰、最直接的断言：这些物质组合体参与了对商业交易的格式化。

Despite its accuracy, the Weberian intuition was long ignored, even if as influential an author as Polanyi does not forget to mention the physical sites in the description he gives of the elements of a market. It came back into force only very recently, in the early 2000s, with work, inspired by science and technology studies

that turned toward concrete markets, aiming to bring out the importance, for their functioning, of things — and therefore of products and procedures — as well as the active role of knowledge, know-how, tools, instruments, or devices.
This new approach, largely unknown, introduced a major discontinuity with previous analyses. One of the main ambitions of this book is to show how interesting and fecund it is.
尽管韦伯的直觉颇为准确，却长期被忽视——即便像波兰尼（Polanyi）这样有影响力的作者，在描述市场要素时也没有忘记提及物理场所。它只是在很近的时期，即2000年代初，才随着受科学技术研究
启发、转向具体市场的研究工作重新生效：这些工作力求揭示物——因而也就是产品与程序——对于市场运作的重要性，以及知识、诀窍、工具、仪器或装置的主动作用。
这一新进路在很大程度上尚不为人知，却与先前的分析造成了重大断裂。本书的主要抱负之一，就是表明它多么有趣、多么富有成果。
THE STRATEGIC PURPOSE OF MARKET AGENCEMENTS

The interface market model evokes the creation of relationships between supplies and demands connected around goods; it describes the transfer of property rights; it refers to competitive behavior and monetary payments. It does not, however, explain how these different actions end up connecting to one another and organizing in such a way as to regularly and successfully produce the observed result: commercial transactions are realized.
市场装配的战略目的
界面市场模型让人想到供给与需求围绕物品而被联结起来的关系的创造；它描述财产权的转移；它指涉竞争行为与货币支付。然而，它并未解释这些不同的行动如何最终彼此连接、并以某种方式组织起来，从而规律而成功地产生所观察到的结果：商业交易得以实现。

Most analysts have understood that in order to account for this constantly renewed miracle, the picture needs to be fleshed out, and more complete models have to be put forward, ones that include in their description the forces that explain why and how this collective-oriented action can emerge. But there are not many answers. Either one considers that it is the agents who, impelled by the calculation of their interests, by their needs, or by any other force or motivation, set markets in motion and keep them animated. Or one imagines that these actions undertaken by agents are fashioned and oriented by norms, rules, systems of social relations or domination, or structures such as the division of labor that channel them toward establishing commercial transactions.

大多数分析者都明白，要解释这一不断更新的奇迹，就必须充实这幅图景，提出更完整的模型，在其描述中纳入那些说明这种具有共同方向的集体行动何以能够涌现、如何涌现的力量。但答案并不多。要么人们认为，是行动者在利益计算、需要或任何其他力量或动机的推动下，启动市场并使之保持活跃。要么人们设想，行动者所采取的行动由规范、规则、社会关系系统或支配系统，或由劳动分工这类把这些行动导向商业交易之建立的结构所塑造和引导。

The notion of agencement, that is to say, a heterogeneous assemblage, putting the accent as it does on the role played by material devices, makes it possible to avoid choosing one or the other of these two solutions. Markets consist of arrangements that play a double role. They contribute to imposing guiding frameworks on individual actions and provide them with motives while channeling collective action toward the conclusion of commercial transactions. Fairs, supermarkets, meeting or matching algorithms, production technologies, calculation and management tools, metrological instruments, advertising campaigns, formulas for establishing prices, brands, the innumerable means for provoking attachments are all devices (which we will explore throughout this book) that format and orient behavior and interactions in an even stronger way than do the supposed human interest or the sole ascendency of rules, norms, laws, or customs or systems of social relations. Market agencements do not exclude any of these forces. Rather, they situate them within the entire set of material and textual devices (including legal coding) that structure and prompt commercial activities.

装配这一概念，也就是说，一种异质的集合体，由于它把重点放在物质装置所扮演的角色上，使人得以避免在两种解决方案之间作出选择。市场由扮演双重角色的安排构成。它们既把引导性框架加诸个体行动并为之提供动机，同时又把集体行动导向商业交易的达成。集市、超市、会面或撮合算法、生产技术、计算与管理工具、计量仪器、广告活动、价格确立的公式、品牌、引发附着的无数手段，都是装置（本书将逐一探索），它们对行为与互动进行格式化并加以引导，其力量甚至强于所谓的人类利益，或规则、规范、法律、习俗或社会关系系统的单独支配。市场装配并不排除这些力量中的任何一种。相反，它把它们安置在整套物质性与文本性装置（包括法律编码）之内，正是这套装置结构并促发商业活动。

One can thus characterize market agencements through their strategic purpose, which is to organize and promote the establishment of bilateral transactions. We will need no fewer than five chapters to explain how they manage this.
因此，我们可以通过市场装配的战略目的来刻画它们，这一目的就是组织并促进双边交易的建立。要解释它们如何做到这一点，我们需要不少于五章的篇幅。
COMPETITION IS THE STRUGGLE TO ESTABLISH BILATERAL TRANSACTIONS . . .

In the market agencement model, what is at stake in competition is establishing transactions. Establishing each new bilateral transaction — one particular seller, one particular good, one particular buyer — is competition’s one and only goal.
竞争是建立双边交易的斗争……
在市场装配模型中，竞争的利害所在是建立交易。建立每一笔新的双边交易——某一个特定的卖家、某一件特定的物品、某一个特定的买家——是竞争唯一的目标。

It may be a radically new transaction, or it may be the renewal of a transaction that has already taken place. Even if buyer and seller seem to have preserved the same identity, and even if the good in question seems very similar to the one that was on offer earlier, it is a different event. The new bilateral transaction is different from the previous ones and cannot, under any circumstances, be considered identical to it or considered to be a mere repetition. The time and place have changed, and with them, in a more or less superficial way, more or less profound, yet real, the identities of the buyer and seller and the qualities of the transferred goods have changed, as well. No transaction is quite like any other. Each must be conquered, and it is precisely for this new conquest that there is competition.

它可能是一笔全新的交易，也可能是对一笔已经发生过的交易的续订。即便买者与卖者似乎保持了相同的身份，即便所涉物品看起来与先前提供的物品极为相似，它仍是一个不同的事件。新的双边交易不同于此前的各笔交易，无论在何种情况下，都不能被视为与之相同，也不能被视为单纯的重复。时间与地点已经改变，随之而来，买者与卖者的身份以及被转移物品的品质，也以或表面或深刻、却真实的方式发生了改变。没有哪笔交易与另一笔完全相同。每一笔都必须被征服，而竞争正是为了这一次新的征服。

In the classical representation of monopoly, a company confiscates the entire supply by having exclusivity over the good, thereby rendering customers captive. Monopoly signifies the absence of competition. In market agencements, under their bilateral form (that is, this buyer, this seller, and this singularized good at this place and at this time),

monopoly is on the contrary the ultimate expression of the competitive struggle. The more a company is able to sideline the agents who might threaten the series of its bilateral monopolies, the more it is able to singularize each of the goods it offers to each of its clients, the more its competitive power is increased.
在对垄断的古典再现中，一家企业通过对物品的排他性占有而攫取全部供给，从而使顾客陷入依附。垄断意味着竞争的缺席。在市场装配中，在其双边形式下（也就是说，这个买家、这个卖家，以及此时此地的这件被独一化的物品），
垄断恰恰相反，是竞争斗争的最高表现。一家企业越是能够把可能威胁其一系列双边垄断的行动者排挤到一边，越是能够把它提供给每一位客户的每一件物品独一化，它的竞争力就越是增强。

This is not a new way of looking at things. It has already been brilliantly illustrated by authors such as Joan Robinson and Edward Chamberlin in the first decades of the twentieth century. In his masterful history of economic analysis, Joseph Schumpeter offers this comment on these two authors: they “allow monopoly to ‘swallow up the competitive analysis’ — every firm being a monopolist, that is, a single seller of its own product.”
Whereas in the traditional conception, monopoly and competition are opposites, according to these two authors, monopoly is the strategy that expresses the logic of competition in its purest form.
The search for monopoly by all available means — this is what drives competition.

And the most radical way to reach it is to impose the singularization not of the good, but of the bilateral transaction itself, in other words, of the trio made up of the one who offers, the one who demands, and the good. In market agencements, perfect competition, which one might call
competitive monopolism
, has nothing to do with that of neoclassical economics. Its only goal is to make bilateral transactions proliferate, and what is at stake is control of that proliferation.
这并不是一种新的看问题方式。20世纪最初几十年，琼·罗宾逊（Joan Robinson）与爱德华·张伯伦（Edward Chamberlin）等作者已经对此作过出色的阐明。约瑟夫·熊彼特（Joseph Schumpeter）在其精湛的经济分析史中，对这两位作者作出如下评论：他们“让垄断‘吞没了竞争分析’——每家企业都是垄断者，也就是说，是其自身产品的唯一卖者。”
而在传统观念中，垄断与竞争彼此对立；按照这两位作者，垄断则是以最纯粹的形式表达竞争逻辑的策略。
用一切可用的手段寻求垄断——这正是驱动竞争的东西。
而达到这一点的最激进方式，是把独一化强加于双边交易本身，而非物品；换言之，强加于由提供者、需求者与物品三者构成的组合。在市场装配中，完全竞争——不妨称之为竞争性垄断（
competitive monopolism
）——与新古典经济学的完全竞争毫无关系。它唯一的目标是使双边交易增殖，而其利害所在是对这种增殖的掌控。
THE PROLIFERATION OF TRANSACTIONS REQUIRES INNOVATION

Innovation is inextricably linked to commercial activity, since the latter consists in establishing bilateral transactions, and each successful transaction rests on its singularization, that is to say, on a specific qualification, however tenuous it may be, and in certain cases, it can be reduced to a mere difference in price of the good sold and bought. If a company does not innovate, it (gradually) excludes itself from commercial activity. In market agencement, innovation is not an exceptional or occasional strategy that agents develop to escape competition or alleviate its rigor. Competition does not stimulate innovation any more than it paralyzes it.

Innovation is the essence of competition. The greater the singularization, that is to say, the greater the scope of the innovation, the more intense is the competition; the weaker it is, that is to say, the more innovation is minor or superficial, the more moderate the competition.

Competition can even effectively disappear when singularization tends toward the imperceptible. If one were not afraid of paradoxical formulations, one might say that in the market agencement model, pure and perfect competition as it is usually described in economics textbooks (a large number of agents offering and seeking the same product) corresponds to a complete extinction of competition and to the long-term collapse of market agencement itself.
交易的增殖要求创新
创新与商业活动不可分割地联系在一起，因为后者在于建立双边交易，而每一笔成功的交易都依赖于其独一化，也就是说，依赖于一种特定的品质界定——无论这界定多么细微；在某些情形下，它可以被化约为所交易物品仅在价格上的差异。一家企业若不创新，就会（逐渐）把自己排除在商业活动之外。在市场装配中，创新并不是行动者为逃避竞争或缓解其严酷而发展出的例外性或偶发性策略。竞争并不刺激创新，正如它也不使创新瘫痪。
创新是竞争的本质。独一化程度越高，也就是说，创新的幅度越大，竞争就越激烈；独一化越弱，也就是说，创新越次要、越表面，竞争就越温和。
当独一化趋于不可察觉时，竞争甚至可以实际上消失。倘若不怕悖论式的表述，人们可以说，在市场装配模型中，经济学教科书通常描述的那种纯粹而完全的竞争（大量行动者提供和寻求同一产品），对应着竞争的彻底熄灭，以及市场装配自身在长期中的崩溃。

In certain forms of commercial organization, the rhythm and depth of innovations, by which I mean the proliferation of bilateral transactions, grow spectacularly. This is referred to as a regime of intensive innovation, which is becoming the rule in activities in the computationally driven tech sector.

This is why the agencement model cannot be shunted aside. In the following chapters, I will put forward numerous examples showing how my model permits us to realistically analyze the way in which merchant activities are linked to the massive mobilization of digital technologies, while the interface model finds itself maladapted to these cases. The personalization and individualization of services, or the made to order (sometimes called “mass customization”), underscores the realism of my concept of competition. The seeming paradox, which is completely comprehensible once we retool our intellectual model, is that singularization strategies, essentially a qualitative pursuit, are the basis of growth, which is expressed quantitatively.
在某些商业组织形式中，创新——我指的是双边交易的增殖——的节奏与深度会以惊人的方式增长。这被称为密集创新体制，它正在成为由计算驱动的科技行业各项活动中的常规。

这正是装配模型不能被搁置一旁的原因。在接下来的几章中，我将提出大量例子，表明我的模型如何使我们能够现实地分析商业活动与数字技术的大规模动员相联结的方式，而界面模型在这些情形中则显得不适应。服务的个性化与个体化，或按订单定制（有时被称为“大规模定制”），凸显了我的竞争概念的现实性。表面上的悖论——一旦我们重新装备自己的思想模型，它便完全可以理解——在于：本质上是质性追求的独一化策略，竟然是（以量来表现的）增长的基础。

Singularization’s central role in commercial transactions is assimilated, in the model, into the concept of innovation. Without innovation, there is no competition, and as a consequence, there is no market activity. And since innovation strategies are diverse, so, too, are the forms of competition.
独一化在商业交易中的核心作用，在模型中被归并到创新这一概念之中。没有创新，就没有竞争，因此也就没有市场活动。而由于创新策略多种多样，竞争的形式也多种多样。

To show that innovation plays just as important a role in slower markets, which seem more traditional and quite different from tech markets, let’s consider the French case of AMAPs, an acronym that translates to “associations for the maintenance of peasant agriculture” (Associations pour le maintien d’une agriculture paysanne).

According to the leaders of the movement, the goal of these associations is not to eliminate the market, but rather to invent new forms of commercial activities. However, as in any market agencement, a threat lurks. There is the danger of producers or consumers switching to other transactions, implying other partners and other goods. For example, the consumer can change producer within the AMAP or turn elsewhere, or the producer might decide to commercialize part of his production in a different way. Within the association, attachments are obtained by organized coprofiling of products, consumers, and producers — that is, by the singularization of each new bilateral transaction. Yet as in any market agencement, attachments can be undone at any moment. Members of the association, whether producers or consumers, can change partners not only within the AMAP, but also by looking for partners outside the AMAP. This is why as a collective market agencement designer, the AMAP relentlessly strives to keep members active and extend membership. It succeeds by constantly reshaping devices of singularization.
为了表明创新在那些更缓慢、显得更传统、与科技市场颇为不同的市场中同样扮演重要角色，让我们考察法国的 AMAP 案例；这个缩写的意思是“维护农民农业协会”（Associations pour le maintien d’une agriculture paysanne）。

据该运动的领导者说，这些协会的目标不是消灭市场，而是发明新的商业活动形式。然而，如同任何市场装配一样，威胁潜伏其间。存在着生产者或消费者转向其他交易的危险，而那意味着其他伙伴与其他物品。例如，消费者可以在 AMAP 内部更换生产者，或转向别处；生产者也可能决定以不同方式销售其部分产品。在协会内部，附着是通过对产品、消费者与生产者进行有组织的共同塑形（coprofiling）而获得的——也就是说，是通过对每一笔新的双边交易进行独一化而获得的。然而，如同任何市场装配，附着随时可能被解除。协会成员，无论是生产者还是消费者，都可以更换伙伴——不仅可以在 AMAP 内部更换，还可以到 AMAP 之外寻找伙伴。正因如此，作为一个集体性的市场装配设计者，AMAP 不懈地努力使成员保持活跃并扩大会员规模。它通过不断重塑独一化装置而获得成功。

This is the reason why AMAPs create frequently revised charters that define and guarantee the qualities of the marketable products (freshness, origin, availability); they introduce new agents; they construct tables detailing delivery sites and frequency, as well as production calendars; they establish rules for decision making; they clarify general principles that define the goals of organized collective action — for example, supporting a new form of agriculture, developing healthy and sustainable foods, and so on.
The association is an agencement that aims to link a group of producers and a group of consumers around duly qualified goods.
这就是为什么 AMAP 会制定频繁修订的章程，以界定并保证可上市产品的品质（新鲜度、产地、可得性）；它们引入新的行动者；它们制作详列配送地点与频率的表格，以及生产日历；它们确立决策规则；它们阐明界定有组织集体行动之目标的一般原则——例如，支持一种新的农业形式，发展健康而可持续的食品，等等。
协会是一种装配，旨在围绕经过恰当品质界定的物品，把一群生产者与一群消费者联结起来。

Although they are often likened to very primitive and almost futureless forms of commercial organizations, AMAPs are sites where innovation that is collectively controlled and decided is central and combines all of the technical, organizational, and social dimensions one usually aims to pry apart. If perchance the goods on offer by an AMAP are not sufficiently singular and convincing, the AMAP will disappear. Indeed, this often happens.
尽管 AMAP 常被比作极为原始、几乎毫无前途的商业组织形式，它们却是这样的场所：在那里，由集体控制并决定的创新居于核心，并把人们通常力图拆开的技术、组织与社会维度结合在一起。倘若某个 AMAP 所提供的物品不够独一、不够有说服力，这个 AMAP 就会消失。事实上，这种情况经常发生。
Without innovation, there are no market agencements of any nature whatsoever. As we will see throughout this book, the rule brooks no exceptions.
没有创新，就没有任何性质的市场装配。正如本书通篇将要表明的，这条规则不容例外。
PROCESS GOODS

If the coprofiling of singular supplies and demands around goods that are themselves singular constitutes the strategic problem that markets must continuously resolve, then it is unrealistic to assume two preexisting blocks of supplies and demands that are independent from one another and that are linked through goods acting as unifying platforms whose origin is considered unproblematic. In other words, if the singularity of a good must be established for each and every transaction, then supply, demand, and the qualities of products do not drive market activity, but are the result achieved by endless activities that constitute and reconstitute an active market agencement.
过程物品
如果围绕本身即为独一的物品，对独一的供给与需求进行共同塑形，构成了市场必须持续解决的战略问题，那么，假设存在两个预先给定、彼此独立的供给与需求块体，它们通过充当统一平台、而其来源被认为不成问题的物品相联结，便是不现实的。换言之，如果物品的独一性必须为每一笔交易而确立，那么，供给、需求与产品的品质就不是驱动市场活动的东西，而是由构成并重新构成一个活跃市场装配的无尽活动所取得的结果。

As goods are transformed throughout the process of design, production, and commercialization, so are the supplies and demands for them. Goods, supplies, and demands are not separate sets; they are intimately connected, caught up in bundles of evolving relationships that ensure otherwise incomprehensible adjustment and adequation. This process can be called
qualification

, which aims at ensuring the coproduction of goods’ characteristics, as well as those of the buyers and sellers, into the activity I refer to as coprofiling. The qualification of goods does not precede the establishment of markets; these activities are at its heart.
物品在设计、生产与商业化过程中被转化，对它们的供给与需求也随之被转化。物品、供给与需求并不是彼此分离的集合；它们紧密相连，卷入一束束演变中的关系，而这些关系确保了否则无法理解的调整与适配。这一过程可以被称为
品质界定
，它旨在确保物品的特征以及买者与卖者的特征共同被生产出来，并汇入我所称的共同塑形活动。物品的品质界定并不先于市场的建立；这些活动正处于市场建立的核心。

The process of qualification is a central feature of all commercial activities, although it has only recently become visible and been laid claim to, because it is becoming hugely amplified in sectors such as the health care, electronic commerce, and service industries. To illustrate, let us take the example of a recognizable mass-market product whose market architecture is reminiscent of an interface market: a model of car with hundreds of thousands sold. A car first exists on a drawing board or in a 3-D digital representation, then as a set of specifications, then as a series of plans and diagrams in a design department, then as a model on a platform, under the as yet vague guise of a concept car, then as a prototype image on glossy paper with its technical annexes, then as a floor model in showrooms put into words by the explanations and rhetoric of the salespeople, then as an object of tests and comparisons in consumer magazines. (An entirely novel set of sequences will need to be added to this account to include autonomous vehicles, which, for example, require lengthy trials in urban situations.)

品质界定过程是所有商业活动的核心特征，尽管它直到晚近才变得可见并被人明确主张，因为它在医疗保健、电子商务与服务业等部门正被极大地放大。为说明这一点，让我们举一个可辨识的大众市场产品为例，其市场架构让人联想到界面市场：一款售出数十万辆的车型。一辆汽车首先存在于绘图板上，或存在于三维数字再现中；然后作为一套规格说明存在；接着作为设计部门中的一系列图纸与图表存在；随后作为平台上的模型、以概念车这一尚且模糊的形态存在；再作为光面纸上的原型图像及其技术附件存在；然后作为展厅里的陈列样车存在，由销售人员的解说与修辞赋予其言辞；最后作为消费者杂志中测试与比较的对象存在。（要把自动驾驶汽车纳入这一叙述，还需要添加一整套全新的序列；例如，它们需要在城市环境中进行长时间的试验。）

After the transaction is concluded, after the car has been purchased and rolls off the lot, it continues to be requalified, to live a life that was not necessarily programmed: it becomes an object of social distinction; it is leased or resold as a secondhand vehicle (which its previous owner may have anticipated by taking care of it and choosing a highly rated model); it is reduced to a wreck whose components are recycled as materials or as spare parts; or it is remanufactured in certain developing countries before leading a second commercial life; or it may eventually be requalified as a classic car.
交易达成之后，在汽车被购买并驶出车场之后，它继续被重新界定品质，过着一种未必被预先规定的生活：它成为社会区分的对象；它被出租，或作为二手车转售（其前任车主可能早已预见到这一点，因而悉心保养，并选择了一款评价很高的车型）；它沦为报废车，其部件作为材料或备件被回收；或者它在某些发展中国家被再制造，随后开始第二次商业生命；又或者，它最终可能被重新界定为老爷车。

The successive requalifications of the product and its concurrent transformations start in design departments or research centers, continue in normalization or certification services, and persist once the transaction has taken place. Each moment of requalification can mobilize a large number of agents. Yet the agents can also be concentrated in one site — for instance, in a marketing department, in which case, a very limited number of agents may be involved. The point is that goods are qualified as a result of some kind of collective and collaborative activity, and the form taken at one moment of commercial transaction is only one of the many forms they will take over the course of their careers. Over the course of this book, I will give numerous examples to illustrate the general nature of this phenomenon.

产品相继的重新界定品质及其同时发生的转化，始于设计部门或研究中心，在标准化或认证服务机构中延续，并在交易发生之后仍然持续。每一个重新界定品质的时刻都可能动员大量行动者。然而，行动者也可能集中于一个场所——例如，集中于一个营销部门，在这种情况下，所涉及的行动者数量可能非常有限。关键在于：物品是在某种集体性、协作性活动的结果中被界定品质的；而它在商业交易某一时刻所采取的形式，只是其生涯中将要采取的众多形式之一。在本书中，我将给出大量例子，以说明这一现象的普遍性。

I hope it is becoming clear why a product must be considered a process. Products are made up of a series of actions, a succession of operations that transform and displace them, passing them from hand to hand through a series of metamorphoses that work out forms judged attractive by economic agents who pay to enjoy their benefits.

Over the course of these metamorphoses, the qualities of products vary. The career of a product has no other purpose than to be transformed into a good, that is, a thing that is sought after, researched, desired, and deserving of being purchased. Marketing, broadly redefined as the concern for getting a product to market, pulls together every single one of the operations that lead to its being involved in a singular commercial transaction. To reduce marketing to superficial operations that aim to make a good desirable to people who have no need for it (Alain Souchon, in his beautiful song, “Foule sentimentale” talks of “desires inflicted on us”) while ignoring the material practices of design and production, is at best a tautology. At worst, it is a sign of completely underestimating the relentless processes by which goods are qualified. My observation applies equally to the AMAP and to chemical or pharmaceutical industries. A product, as Chamberlin underlines, is an economic variable like any other.
我希望，为什么产品必须被视为一个过程，这一点正变得清楚。产品由一系列行动构成，由一连串操作构成，这些操作转化并移动产品，使它在一系列变形中从一只手传到另一只手；这些变形打造出被经济行动者判定为有吸引力的形式，而他们付钱以享受其益处。

在这些变形过程中，产品的品质不断变化。产品的生涯没有别的目的，就是被转化为物品，也就是说，转化为一种被追寻、被探究、被欲求、值得被购买的东西。营销——若宽泛地重新界定为让产品进入市场的关切——汇集了导致产品卷入某一独一商业交易的全部操作。把营销化约为一些表面操作——旨在让一件物品对并不需要它的人显得可欲（阿兰·苏雄（Alain Souchon）在他那首优美的歌《感伤的人群》（“Foule sentimentale”）中谈到“强加给我们的欲望”）——同时无视设计与生产的物质实践，这至多是一种同义反复。最坏的情况下，这标志着对物品借以被界定品质的那些不懈过程的彻底低估。我的观察同样适用于 AMAP，也适用于化学或制药产业。正如张伯伦所强调的，产品与任何其他东西一样，是一个经济变量。
PROLIFERATING AGENTS, PLASTIC IDENTITIES, AND NETWORKING

Unlike the platform good in the interface model, the process good articulates supplies and demands. If it did not, it would not warrant the name “market good.” This articulation, however, is an action that involves a series of modifications and adaptations that connect design, production, and circulation activities to one another. The action must mobilize multiple agents to collectively engage in the creation, manufacturing, sale, and use of these products.
增殖的行动者、可塑的身份与网络化
与界面模型中的平台物品不同，过程物品接合供给与需求。如果它不这样做，就不配“市场物品”之名。然而，这种接合是一种行动，涉及一系列修改与适配，把设计、生产与流通活动彼此连接起来。这一行动必须动员多个行动者，共同参与这些产品的创造、制造、销售与使用。

Understood in this broadened vision, the list of agents enrolled in commercial activity stretches well beyond the usual roles imagined by the notions of supply and demand in the interface market model. It includes, for instance, researchers, some of whom work in university laboratories, others in industrial research centers, engineers, civil servants and experts in competition policy, and bankers prompted to invest in new lines of activity; it involves users or consumers (individual or collective), governmental agencies, lawyers, professional associations, unions, and even certification bodies. These multiple agents, who vary from sector to sector, are likely to be involved at one moment or another, in one capacity or another, in the qualification or requalification of a good where the only horizon of their action is the potential commercialization of that good. Agents generally come from state spheres as much as from civil society, and indeed, there is no reason to draw a categorical distinction between the two. All of the various activities whose objective is to find a market for goods should be included in the market.

在这种扩展了的视野中理解，被纳入商业活动的行动者名单远远超出界面市场模型中供给与需求概念所设想的通常角色。例如，它包括研究者——其中一些人在大学实验室工作，另一些人在工业研究中心工作——工程师、公务员与竞争政策专家，以及被促动投资于新活动领域的银行家；它涉及使用者或消费者（个体的或集体的）、政府机构、律师、专业协会、工会，甚至认证机构。这些形形色色的行动者因部门而异，他们很可能在某个时刻、以某种身份，参与某件物品的品质界定或重新界定品质；而他们行动的唯一地平线，就是该物品潜在的商业化。行动者一般既来自国家领域，也同样来自公民社会；事实上，没有理由在两者之间划出范畴性的区分。所有以替物品找到市场为目标的各种活动，都应当被纳入市场。

It does not therefore make sense to refer to two intertwined populations, or even to two independent populations of buyers and sellers. The essential notion here is networks. Not the familiar social networks linking agents whose identities are stabilized, but networks that, as we will see, cross all the different populations involved in commercial activities. Within these networks, goods, agents, and material infrastructures are caught up in the same dynamic, where they are subject to being transformed while coevolving.
Along these networks, the qualities of products and the identities of people are reworked until they get adjusted to one another.
因此，谈论两个相互交织的人群，甚至谈论两个彼此独立的买者与卖者人群，都没有意义。这里的关键概念是网络。不是那种连接身份已稳定化的行动者的熟悉社会网络，而是——正如我们将看到的——横贯参与商业活动的所有不同人群的网络。在这些网络内部，物品、行动者与物质基础设施卷入同一动态，在共同演化中经受转化。
沿着这些网络，产品的品质与人的身份被反复加工，直到彼此相适配。

To put it in a nutshell, while the interface market model, which describes markets as organizations structured around groups of agents and platform goods, has neither thickness nor depth, the image of commercial activities that prevails in the market agencement model is temporal and longitudinal.
简而言之，界面市场模型把市场描述为围绕行动者群体与平台物品而组织起来的组织，它既无厚度也无深度；而在市场装配模型中占主导的商业活动形象，则是时间性的、纵向的。
This requalification has important consequences for the relations between markets and societies. Max Weber speaks of “consociation” to designate the form of social relations instituted by markets.

A particular form of socialization, consociation results from the instauration of competition, which is the simplest modality of coordination that leads an actor to take another into account. According to Weber, the market generates social relations, or, if you prefer, sociability, through competition. Weber thus breaks with the classical point of view articulated by Adam Smith: “Two greyhounds, in running down the same hare, have sometimes the appearance of acting in some sort of concert. Each turns her [the hare being hunted] toward his companion, or endeavors to intercept her when his companion turns her toward himself. This, however, is not the effect of any contract, but of the accidental concurrence of their passions in the same object at that particular time.”

Yet contrary to what Smith imagined, effective competition does not require isolated agents with only the contingent convergence of their desires connecting them. But neither is consociation reducible to a simple coordination. As Weber would have it, competition is born of collective work, constantly renewed and necessary to the establishment of bilateral transactions.

The coproduction of supplies, demands, and goods — which has to somehow handle the concerns and contestations it provokes — is at the heart of the commercial dynamic. It implies establishing collaborative relations, organizing negotiations, setting decisional processes into motion, structuring and reconfiguring networks. It does not work through rarifying relations; it organizes their proliferation.
这种重新界定对市场与社会之间的关系具有重要后果。马克斯·韦伯谈到“联合体化”（consociation），用以指称市场所建制的那种社会关系形式。

作为一种特殊的社会化形式，联合体化源于竞争的创设；竞争是最简单的协调方式，它使一个行动者把另一个行动者纳入考虑。按照韦伯，市场通过竞争产生社会关系，或者若愿意这样说，产生社会性。韦伯由此与亚当·斯密（Adam Smith）所表述的古典观点决裂：“两条猎犬追逐同一只野兔时，有时看起来像是在协同行动。每一只都把野兔（即被追逐的那只）赶向自己的同伴，或者在同伴把野兔赶向自己时竭力拦截它。然而，这并不是任何契约的结果，而只是它们的激情在同一时刻偶然汇聚于同一对象。”
然而，与斯密的设想相反，有效的竞争并不需要彼此孤立、仅靠其欲望的偶然汇聚而相连的行动者。但联合体化也不能被化约为单纯的协调。按照韦伯的看法，竞争诞生于集体工作，这种工作不断更新，并且是建立双边交易的必要条件。
供给、需求与物品的共同生产——它必须设法应对自身所引发的关切与争议——处于商业动态的核心。它意味着建立协作关系、组织谈判、启动决策过程、结构化并重构网络。它并不通过使关系变得稀少来运作；它组织关系的增殖。

Market activities engender social relations, but not just any social relations. They also manufacture impersonal relations, but not exclusively. One of this book’s objectives is to further characterize this double process.
市场活动产生社会关系，但不是随便什么社会关系。它们也制造非人格的关系，但并非只制造这种关系。本书的目标之一，就是进一步刻画这一双重过程。
CHAPTER SUMMARIES: UNDERSTANDING MARKETS AS FRAMINGS
各章概要：把市场理解为框定

Now that the major traits that distinguish market agencements from other possible conceptions of the market have been identified (that is, the interface market), we can turn to analyzing the way they function. How does collective action lead to the production of bilateral transactions? How does it renew and extend them?
既然已经辨识出那些使市场装配区别于其他可能的市场构念的主要特征（也就是说，区别于界面市场），我们现在可以转向分析它们如何运作。集体行动如何导向双边交易的生产？它又如何更新并扩展这些交易？
To answer these questions, I will now introduce the notion of
framing (cadrage
) which refers to the devices that orient and structure action toward its strategic goal.

In the case of market agencements, I suggest marking out five framings. I will devote one chapter to each framing, each of which corresponds to a different operation that, when combined with the others, prepares and formats commercial transactions. Distinguishing five types of framings does not imply these are naturally distinct sites or a chronological development. These framings are, as we will see, multisited and open to back-andforth. What follows is a brief overview of the rest of the book. The agencement model begins by empirically observing that for the market transaction to take place, there must first be a split between the goods that will be the object of a market transaction at some moment of their existence and the agencies capable of evaluating and appreciating the goods that will pass through their hands at another point in time. It may seem counterintuitive, but the entities capable of evaluating a good at first are not the potential future buyers. They are in fact the groups involved in creating it and acting as provisional and tentative spokespeople for them. What it entails for agents to be split from the good is to do work to create the conditions for the good to be widely evaluated and eventually requalified. The examples to come will help to clarify this unusual starting point.
为回答这些问题，我现在要引入
框定（cadrage
）这一概念，它指的是那些把行动导向其战略目标并为之赋予结构的装置。

就市场装配而言，我建议划定五种框定。我将为每一种框定各写一章，每一种框定都对应一种不同的操作，这些操作与其他操作结合起来，便准备并格式化商业交易。区分五种框定，并不意味着它们天然就是彼此分离的场所，也不意味着它们构成一种按时间顺序展开的发展过程。我们将会看到，这些框定是多场所的，并且允许来回往复。以下是对本书其余部分的简要概览。装配模型首先从经验观察出发：市场交易要得以发生，首先必须在物品与能动者之间有一道分离——物品在其存在的某一时刻将成为市场交易的对象，而能动者则能够在另一个时间点评价并赏识那些将经过其手中的物品。这乍看似乎有悖直觉：最初有能力评价一件物品的实体，并不是潜在的未来买家。事实上，它们是参与创造该物品的群体，并临时地、试探性地充当未来买家的代言人。行动者与物品相分离，这意味着要付出工作，为物品被广泛评价并最终重新界定品质创造条件。后面的例子将有助于澄清这一不寻常的起点。

Introducing this split between goods and their evaluation, which appears most clearly at the moment of transaction itself, is the result of many stages of work, beginning at the moment of the good’s conception. Chapters 2 and 3 present two framings that organize this separation. The first framing has the function of formatting the entities designed to be marketed. To designate this little-studied process, I invoke a neologism,
market-oriented passiva(c)tion
, which
a) detaches the good and liberates it from all those who participated in its elaboration and profiling,
b) renders it apt to provoke courses of actions and to contribute to their realization (that is, imbues it with uses),
c) ensures that its behavior is at least to a certain extent controllable and predictable, and
d) organizes the attribution and transfer of property rights.

It is worth noting that the investments necessary for market-oriented passiva(c)tion are all the greater, more expensive, and more complex as the entities that must be transformed into commercial goods are close to the living world or include living beings.
引入物品与其评价之间的这一分离——它在交易发生的时刻表现得最为清楚——是许多阶段工作的结果，而这些工作始于物品被构想之时。第2章和第3章呈现组织这一分离的两种框定。第一种框定的功能，是格式化那些被设计用来投放市场的实体。为指称这一鲜有人研究的过程，我启用一个新词——
面向市场的被动化
（passiva(c)tion）：
a）使物品脱离并摆脱所有参与其研制与特征刻画的人；
b）使物品适于引发行动过程并有助于这些过程的实现（也就是说，赋予其用途）；
c）确保物品的行为至少在一定程度上可控、可预测；
d）组织财产权的归属与转移。
值得注意的是，必须被转化为商业物品的实体越是接近生命世界或包含生命体，面向市场的被动化所需的投入就越大、越昂贵、越复杂。

The successive transformations through which the future good passes coincide with it being evaluated. The evaluations, which feed and orient the qualification process, suppose a second series of framings that will ensure that the agencies formatted to carry out these evaluation operations are getting the job done. The evaluating agencies, which can be individuals or collective entities such as a consumer group or company, must have the equipment at their disposal without which they cannot do their work. This includes know-how, manuals, comparative guides, accounting tools, management instruments, cost-benefit analysis methods, data, algorithms, and so on.
未来物品所经历的一系列相继转化，与它被评价的过程同时发生。这些评价滋养并引导品质界定的过程，它们预设了第二组框定，用以确保那些被格式化以执行这些评价操作的能动者确实完成了工作。评价能动者可以是个体，也可以是诸如消费者团体或公司之类的集体实体；它们必须拥有可供支配的装备，没有这些装备，它们就无法完成工作。这些装备包括诀窍、手册、比较指南、会计工具、管理工具、成本—收益分析方法、数据、算法，等等。

If what I am describing as yet sounds obscure, just remember that the model of interface markets forgoes taking all the formatting I am describing into account. It simply presumes that pass(act)ivated goods and agencies that evaluate them are available, ready made, and lie outside the analysis of markets. Yet, as my research, along with that of others, shows, in concrete markets, making goods pass(act)ive and populating the marketplace with evaluating agencies directly contributes to spurring commercial activity.

Making this happen requires mobilizing considerable material, legal, and discursive means to ensure that throughout the conception, production, and commercialization process, the objects involved will indeed do what they are supposed to do and that the different agents involved have the tools and instruments they need to evaluate the goods at their disposal. (As an example, think of the controversy around the safety of self-driving vehicles.) That is to say, at each point in the qualification process, agents should be able to envision how sellers and buyers will value the good and consequently decide how it might be transformed.
如果我此刻描述的东西听起来仍然晦涩，只需记住：界面市场模型放弃把我所描述的这一切格式化纳入考量。它只是预设，被动化—激活的物品以及评价它们的能动者都是现成可得的，并且处于市场分析之外。然而，正如我的研究以及其他人的研究所表明的，在具体的市场中，使物品被动化—激活、并让评价能动者充实市场，直接有助于激发商业活动。
要做到这一点，就必须调动大量物质的、法律的与话语的手段，以确保在整个构想、生产与商业化过程中，所涉对象确实会做它们本该做的事，并且所涉的不同行动者都拥有评价其手中物品所需的工具与器械。（举例来说，可以想想围绕自动驾驶汽车安全性的争议。）也就是说，在品质界定过程的每一点上，行动者都应当能够预见卖者与买者将如何评价该物品，并据此决定它可以如何被转化。

It is not, however, enough for the goods to be made pass(act)ive and for a set of agencies to be given the capacity to evaluate and transform them. It is also necessary that certain agencies agree to pay to acquire the goods they are being offered. Two extra series of framings contribute to this result. The first framing orchestrates encounters between process goods as their form successively changes and the different agencies involved in their qualification-singularization. These encounters can happen at any stage of the good’s career. The second framing organizes the attachment of the goods to potential buyers in such a way as to obtain the latter’s willingness to pay.
然而，仅仅使物品被动化—激活、并让一组能动者获得评价和转化物品的能力，还不够。还必须有一些能动者同意支付，以取得向他们提供的物品。另外两组框定促成这一结果。第一种框定编排过程物品——其形态依次变化——与参与其品质界定—独一化的不同能动者之间的相遇。这些相遇可以发生在物品生涯的任何一个阶段。第二种框定则组织物品与潜在买者之间的附着，以获取后者的支付意愿。

Chapter 4 will present the devices required to orchestrate all of these encounters. These devices have technical-material components such as matching algorithms, trade shows and fairs, congresses and conferences, corner stores and malls, window displays, directories, supermarket carts, internet sites and their web interfaces, and more. They also have textual and audiovisual components (advertising messages, clips, brochures) and human components (intermediaries, consultants, technology-transfer agencies, salespeople, influencers, customer service, and so on).
第4章将呈现为编排所有这些相遇所需的装置。这些装置具有技术—物质性的组成部分，例如匹配算法、贸易展与博览会、行业大会与会议、街角小店与购物中心、橱窗陈列、名录、超市购物车、互联网站点及其网络界面，等等。它们还具有文本与视听性的组成部分（广告信息、短片、宣传册）以及人的组成部分（中间人、顾问、技术转移机构、销售人员、网络红人、客户服务，等等）。

Market devices aim to capture potential customers’ attention and to make them deviate from their original trajectories, just like the street sellers calling out on the sidewalk in London. This is not enough, however. Imagine a framing of encounters that awakens curiosity, fires up desire, excites the passions, amplifies and transforms these into interest, and yet ultimately fails to obtain the willingness to pay. Payment can be obtained only if the good ends up attached to the client and the client to the good. That is to say, the process of singularization must go so far as to make the good and the agent reciprocally constitutive of one another. This is the aim of the fourth series of framings, which will be presented in Chapter 5. Carrying out the labor of incorporation, which has more to do with affect than it does with interests, uses, or needs, requires even more devices.

市场装置旨在抓住潜在顾客的注意力，使他们偏离原本的轨迹，就像伦敦人行道上大声招徕的街头卖家一样。然而，这还不够。设想一种相遇的框定：它唤起好奇、点燃欲望、激发激情，把这些激情放大并转化为兴趣，最终却未能获得支付意愿。只有当物品最终附着于顾客、顾客也附着于物品时，支付才能被获得。也就是说，独一化的过程必须一直推进到使物品与行动者彼此互为构成条件。这正是第四组框定的目标，第5章将予以呈现。纳入的劳动（labor of incorporation）更关乎情动，而非利益、用途或需求，完成这种劳动需要更多的装置。

Once the process of attachment is well under way, the final step is to transform the ongoing attachment into a willingness to pay while at the same time setting the price of the good that is the object of the transaction. In market agencements, establishing the price is not mechanically determined by a confrontation between two blocks, supply and demand. It is the result of the particular activities, analyzed in Chapter 6, that constitute what I have called “price formulation.” Price formulation is based on both qualitative and quantitative operations. It connects the particular conditions of the transaction to more general evaluations, such that the price becomes a variable that qualifies the good and contributes to its singularization. These activities require appropriate devices that draw on the skills and know-how of a great number of actors who mobilize research tools and sophisticated calculations. They are at the heart of the power relations enacted by commercial practices.

一旦附着的过程顺利展开，最后一步就是把持续中的附着转化为支付意愿，与此同时为作为交易对象的物品设定价格。在市场装配中，价格的确立并非由供给与需求这两个块体之间的对峙机械地决定。它是第6章所分析的那些特定活动的结果，这些活动构成了我所谓的“价格构式”。价格构式建立在定性与定量两类操作之上。它把交易的特定条件与更为一般的评价连接起来，使价格成为一个界定物品品质、并有助于其独一化的变量。这些活动需要恰当的装置，而这些装置依托众多行动者的技能与诀窍，他们调动研究工具并进行复杂的计算。这些活动处于商业实践所实施的权力关系的核心。

The five framings entail engaging with, investing in, and implementing an array of devices that structure the various activities that will lead to the proliferation of bilateral transactions. It all comes down to a series of goaloriented actions —
a) rendering goods pass(act)ive;
b) activating agencies capable of evaluating and transforming these goods;
c) organizing their encounter;
d) ensuring the attachment of the goods to the agencies;
e) obtaining consent to pay; and
f) setting a price and compelling payment–actions that combine and interweave with one another, with possible feedback loops and iterations.
这五种框定意味着要接触、投入并实施一系列装置，这些装置为各种活动赋予结构，而这些活动将导致双边交易的增殖。归根结底，这是一系列目标导向的行动——
a）使物品被动化—激活；
b）激活有能力评价并转化这些物品的能动者；
c）组织它们的相遇；
d）确保物品附着于能动者；
e）获得支付的同意；
f）设定价格并强制支付——这些行动彼此结合、交织，并可能有反馈回路与反复迭代。
Market agencements are constantly dealing with forces that provoke them to reformulate and reformat themselves. This constant
reagencing
can ultimately even put their strategic goal into question.
Analysis of how agencements function is therefore not distinct from analysis of their transformations.
市场装配不断地与各种力量打交道，这些力量促使它们重构自身、重新格式化自身。这种持续的
重新装配
最终甚至可能使其战略目标本身成为问题。
因此，对装配如何运作的分析，与对其转变的分析不可分割。

The dramatic expansion of market agencements today is examined in Chapter 7, which also explores the different trajectories they are liable to follow and dwells on the way they combine market and nonmarket activities.
第7章考察市场装配在今日的急剧扩张，同时也探讨它们可能遵循的不同轨迹，并详述它们如何把市场活动与非市场活动结合起来。

Chapter 8, which concludes the book, introduces the question of political engineering to the analysis of market agencements. One of the expected benefits of the method followed here, and in fact its only justification, is indeed that it offers new perspectives on the following question: Can one organize market activities not so that they embody an ideal invented by experts in the quiet of their consulting companies’ offices, but rather so that they also respond to the demands of a precise set of specifications that, following a debate, establish objectives and their priorities?
作为全书结论的第8章，把政治工程的问题引入对市场装配的分析。此处所循方法的一项预期收益——事实上也是它唯一的正当理由——确实在于：它为下述问题提供了新的视角：人们能否这样组织市场活动——不是让市场活动体现专家在其咨询公司办公室的安静角落里发明出来的理想，而是让它们同时回应一套精确规格的要求，这套规格经过辩论，确立各项目标及其优先次序？

The answer to this question will require a subsequent book. First, however, a problem has to be solved. Imagine that specifications for a market have been defined and approved. Is it realistic to imagine that one can move from ideas directly to concrete devices without the project falling apart and drifting again and again? It is one thing to put propositions on the table, to formulate orientations. Implementing them is something else altogether. The final chapter examines specific examples — financial markets, the economies of climate change and genetically modified plants — to figure out the strategy that should be followed and to show how, at some points, ideas can impinge upon framings (for example, theoretical models or intuitions, expectations, legal considerations) and thus can be shown to act on the architecture of market agencements and their functioning. The notion of market agencement I have developed provides a general framework for the description of market activities. The model makes it possible to grasp the unity of the market order while maintaining the diversity of its possible configurations. There is no other theoretical formulation that I know of that takes into account all five of the framings presented here or the way they are articulated with one another. The objective of this book is to fill this lacuna. To this end, I will rely equally on work carried out by social scientists and by professionals in commercial activities, whoever they may be. My only and basic goal is better analyzing market practices and how they cause matters of concern. At this stage, I will not propose any agencements as correctives in an uneasy world. I will instead simply consider a number of useful studies that, despite their diversity and sometimes their opposition to one another, contain potential contributions toward the gradual exploration of a model that none of them explicitly envisage, but that taken together, they suggest. At stake is the possibility of properly understanding markets so as to better identify the means of transforming them.

对这个问题的回答将需要另一本书。然而，首先必须解决一个问题。设想某个市场的规格已经得到界定并获批准。设想人们能够从理念直接走向具体装置，而项目不会一再瓦解、一再漂移——这现实吗？把命题摆上桌面、提出方向，是一回事；实施它们则完全是另一回事。最后一章考察具体的例子——金融市场、围绕气候变化与转基因植物形成的经济活动——以弄清应当遵循何种策略，并表明观念如何在某些节点上作用于框定（例如理论模型或直觉、预期、法律考量），从而可以被证明作用于市场装配的架构及其运作。我所发展的市场装配概念为描述市场活动提供了一个总体框架。该模型使人能够把握市场秩序的统一性，同时保持其可能配置的多样性。据我所知，没有其他理论表述考虑到了此处呈现的全部五种框定，或它们彼此衔接的方式。本书的目标正是填补这一空白。为此，我将同样依靠社会科学家与商业活动专业人士所作的工作，无论他们是谁。我唯一的基本目标，是更好地分析市场实践以及它们如何引发关切事项。在这个阶段，我不会提出任何装配作为动荡世界中的矫正方案。相反，我将只是考察若干有用的研究；这些研究尽管彼此不同，有时甚至相互对立，却包含着潜在贡献，有助于逐步探索一个它们中没有任何一个明确设想过、但合在一起却暗示出来的模型。关键在于：能否恰当地理解市场，从而更好地辨识转变市场的手段。

As we reach the end of this introductory chapter, it is my hope that the reader will be convinced to join me in this adventure. Before getting on board, you should know that in order to demonstrate the generality of the model, the cases presented have been chosen from a wide variety of sectors. For obvious reasons, for the length of the journey, I will accord a special place to the technologies and know-how developed by the companies that populate Silicon Valley, some of which have imposed their way on the world at large. They achieve these ends by conceiving of tools, equipment, devices, and infrastructures that reinforce and render even more performant the framings of market agencements — which explains their success, all while rendering them more noticeable. As a consequence, markets are now easier to analyze and debate.

在作为引论的本章接近尾声时，我希望读者已被说服，愿意与我一同踏上这场冒险。在上船之前，你应当知道：为证明该模型的普遍性，书中所呈现的案例选自极为多样的部门。出于显而易见的原因，在接下来的整个讨论过程中，我将给予硅谷那些公司所开发的技术与诀窍一个特殊位置——其中一些公司已把自己的方式强加于整个世界。它们通过构想工具、设备、装置与基础设施来达到这些目的，这些造物强化市场装配的框定，并使之更加高效——这解释了它们的成功，同时也使这些框定更加显眼。其结果是，如今的市场更容易被分析、也更容易被讨论。

For more precise definition of the term “passiva(c)tion,” see Chapter 2. The word has been chosen to highlight that a good must simultaneously respond to two imperatives, between which it must find an equilibrium. On the one side, activation — the good must be capable of eliciting and contributing to new courses of action. On the other side, what could be called “passification” — the good must be amenable to control and must remain predictable.
